Micrometer is a compile dependency; the OTel API is `optional`, so a host that does not enable tracing pays nothing. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath — shipped in the Spring Boot starter (`static/_pathland/`) and the Quarkus extension (`META-INF/resources/_pathland/`) — resolving through the thread context classloader first so an application-supplied override wins; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory). - Topic fan-out is node-local: `PathlandSignalHub` routes to this process's sessions only. A Redis/pub-sub-backed hub (each node fanning out to its local sessions) is a follow-up; the topic name + subject are the stable wire keys. - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. +- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: the session records the viewport but + does not expose it to views (`Platform.VIEWPORT`); SSR still emits the app's + full tree, and `VISIBLE_RANGE` input is not routed to a lazy window. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: starts with a `META::PING` readiness probe, waits for the origin's transport-level `META::PONG`, then sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC` (the probe avoids racing the origin's `@OnOpen`/session wiring), **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. A lost probe/`RESYNC` is retried from the proxy scheduler starting at 50 ms and backing off to 500 ms until the snapshot arrives, so a lost first handshake cannot consume the whole SSR budget. The service credential + a cycle-guard instance id ride the handshake headers. **Backpressure** (spec/PROXY.md §8): a "chatty origin" breaker (a per-second batch cap → drop + `RESYNC`) and event coalescing (pointer-moves coalesce by target; discrete events flush immediately). - **`proxy.ProxyHost`** — one `ProxySession` per `PROXY_VIEW` node, each with its own block; routes inbound events whose target is in a proxy range to the owning origin connection; owns the proxy scheduler. `reconcile(wanted)` starts a session for every `PROXY_VIEW` node and closes the session of every node that left the tree; released id blocks go to a **free-block pool** and are reused, so repeated removal/re-add cycles never exhaust the 1024-block range. - **`PathlandSession`** integration — captures `RenderResult.proxyViews()` and registers the emitter's structural-reconcile callback (`Emitter.onStructureReconciled`) to `reconcileProxies()`, so a proxy lives **exactly while its node is in the retained tree** (spec/PROXY.md §7): a `SizeThatFits` slot dropping the candidate that held it closes the origin connection, and re-adding it opens a fresh one (re-seeded by `META::RESYNC`). The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not in the DOM); eliminating it needs the `ProxySession` to track the ids it emitted and `DELETE` them on close. ## Verified by `mvn test` — `PathlandSessionTest`: mounts + routes taps through the binding maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other), and **message-before-open ordering** (environment/resync that race `open` still attach the connection and emit the snapshot). `TopicsTest`: strongly typed `(topic, subject)` routing (customer 43 never sees customer 42's update), every session for a subject updates, global topics reach only subscribed sessions and stay isolated from a same-named scoped topic, rapid publishes coalesce latest-wins, updates run on the session actor, close removes subscriptions, unsubscribe keeps the last value, and a topic outside a session fails on read. `PathlandHostTest`: longest-prefix dispatch + route stripping, mount-boundary respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxyIdMapTest`: the reserved range, block round-trips, overflow rejection, and the opcode remap (TREE/PARAMETER node ids remapped, APPEND/META untouched, EVENT targets unmapped). `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the PING/PONG readiness probe followed by ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC and the handshake headers, PING retry while the origin is not ready, snapshot retry when the first RESYNC is lost, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame rebases its string offsets (SET_TEXT / LIST / STRING operands) and returns the base unchanged when there is  # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 12, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
 signals/computed/effects, router, cross-platform state, and the
 `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. The opcode/wire layer
 (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`) lives in the
 pure-Java `pathland-core` module, which this module depends on. Server and
 renderer modules depend on this module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored
 views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in
 `pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image
 build) carries no JNA.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Opcode/wire layer**: moved to the `pathland-core` module
   (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`). The DSL
   still re-exports the same behaviour through `Text(...)` and the emitter.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly
   typed `Topic<T, S>` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also
   `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)`
   declares an unscoped `Topic<T, GlobalSubject>` with the two-argument
   `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal<T>` backed by a
   session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and
   applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local,
   installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes
   `unsubscribe` and `submit`. Resolution is lazy when a root view's field
   initializer runs before the context is installed.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop**: moved to `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore`),
   so server runtimes do not pull JNA.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its
   real parent (not the tree root), so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a
   pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal/state and Kotlin DSL tests
   (which exercise the emitter end-to-end); `pathland-core` owns the
   protocol-manifest, frame-codec, and Markdown tests.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `topic(key, subject, initial)`, `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`,
   `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Verification gaps
 
 - **Media swap coverage (MEDIA-COVERAGE-001):** `MediaProjectionTest` covers
   root projection, surface-first binding, root-rerender identity, and transport
   targeting. It does not establish every structural-swap frame invariant or
   native playback continuity. See the
   [traceability pilot audit](../../../docs/audits/media-controller-identity.md).
 
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` still
+  materialize all children eagerly. The `ForEach` data source, extent
+  inference, engine-owned window, keyed window reconcile,
+  `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/`FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` emission, and `VISIBLE_RANGE`
+  input routing are not implemented.
+
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-core` is the pure-Java opcode/wire leaf: protocol, frame codec,
   events, opcode sink, attributed text, and Markdown.
 - `pathland-view-core` is the Kotlin engine + DSL module: signal/state/router,
   the `View` SPI and value types, the retained-tree emitter, and
   `dev.pathland.view.dsl`. It depends on `pathland-core`.
 - `core`/`engine`/`dsl` remain logical subpackages inside `pathland-view-core`,
   with a few deliberate intra-module references (`Color`/`MediaController`/
   `Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting the engine out would still
   require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on both modules. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 # pathland-core-transport — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** September 3, 2026
 
 The **transport** layer: the shared-memory ring owner and the network batch
 codec (both directions). Protocol contract: `spec/OPCODE.md` (Transport).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **`RingTransport`**: zero-copy SPSC shared-memory transport over the
   `pathland-core` linear memory — `next_frame` (guest→host frames as
   `OpcodeBatch`) and `send_input`/`drain_events` (host→guest raw inputs,
   including shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` text via the host event arena).
 - **Network batch codec** (`batch.rs`, `net.rs`): `encode_batch`/`decode_batch`
   for guest→host frames and `encode_events`/`decode_events` for host→guest
   event batches (`HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag, `TEXT_CHANGED` text in the
   batch string section, `Navigate` URLs in the string section, plus all typed
   draft events — focus/edit/submit/scroll/wheel/date-changed). Both directions
   are fully wired at the codec level.
 - **Message sequence** (`sequence`, header offset 8): the batch header carries a
   per-stream monotonic **message sequence** (the network transport's loss
   detector; `Batch::sequence()`). The `Batcher` owns the counter and increments
   it once per flushed batch; heartbeat/request batches carry `0`. Consumers
   detect a gap and recover with a full snapshot (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap
   detection).
 - **Batching policy** (`batching.rs`): time/size flush thresholds with arena
   delta tracking.
 - **Conformance vectors 13/14/19** (`conformance.rs`): golden network-batch
   bytes — incl. **vector 19** (a `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` with the
   `"color.primary"` arena delta).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - No out-of-the-box duplex *server transport* (WebSocket/session plumbing) in
   this crate — the codecs exist; the Java demos (Quarkus/Spring) wire the
   browser↔server duplex.
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: the `VISIBLE_RANGE` event (0x15) is
+  specified but not encoded/decoded, and no conformance vector covers it yet.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-core-transport` — ring round-trips (incl. zero-copy),
 batch encode/decode both directions, batching policy, conformance vectors.

 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **protocol core**: 16-byte opcode, SPSC ring buffers (both directions),
 bump arenas (both directions), memory layout, typed events, and the golden
 conformance vectors. The protocol contract is defined in `spec/`; this file

   `TEXT 0x01, IMAGE 0x02, COLOR 0x03, SHAPE 0x04, DIVIDER 0x05, SPACER 0x06,
   PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07, GAUGE 0x08, VIDEO 0x0A, ICON 0x0B, VSTACK 0x10, HSTACK 0x11, ZSTACK 0x12, GRID

   `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D),
   `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E); the `MEDIA_*` events target the **controller** id and add

   spec/MEDIA.md); `ICON_NAME` (0x1038,
   STRING — the `ICON` primitive's canonical name, spec/ICONS.md); plus the navigation
   drafts `TRANSITION` (0x1031), `ROUTE` (0x2019, STRING), `NAV_DEPTH` (0x201A,
   U32 — the `NavigationContainer`'s back-stack depth, so native navigation
   adapters reconcile their page stack by depth) and `NAV_CHROME` (0x201B,
   F32-enum chrome mode: `PlatformDefault`=0 / `Custom`=1 — the renderer
   supplies default navigation chrome, or the developer owns all nav UI)).
 - **`ICON` vocabulary** (`constants::icon`): the canonical `ICON_NAME` names
   (spec/ICONS.md) as `&str` consts + `NAMES` + `is_canonical` — the protocol
   vocabulary only; the canonical-name → native-glyph mapping is renderer-owned
   (GTK + web each define their own).
 - **Attributed text** (`PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`, `0x05`) +
   `AttributedString` model/codec: text + UTF-8-byte range style runs (v1:
   `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`COLOR`/`FONT_STYLE`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`UNDERLINE`/
   `STRIKETHROUGH`) + links, arena payload encode/decode, `Guest::set_attributed_text`,
   and overlap-resolving `segments()`. Covered by conformance vector 46.
 - **Commands**: `TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move (append = `u32::MAX`);
   `PARAMETER` `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`/`SET_TEXT`/`SET_DATE`/
   `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`; `META`
   `RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT`/`RESYNC`. **`META::PING`/`PONG`** (0x04/0x05) are the
   transport-liveness heartbeat — **network batch transport only** (a shared-memory
   ring consumer MUST NOT emit/expect/relay them); the core engine never produces
   them. `META::ENVIRONMENT` is the extensible
   platform-environment field family (`environment::VIEWPORT_WIDTH`/
   `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT`/`ROUTE` — the `ROUTE` string uses the `TEXT_CHANGED`/
   `NAVIGATE` dual convention).
 - **Typed `Event` enum**: pointer/key/value/text events (0x01–0x07) plus the
   draft `FocusChanged`, `EditingChanged`, `Submit`, `Scroll`, `Wheel`,
   `DateChanged` (0x08–0x0D) and `Navigate` (0x0E) — all encode/decode
   round-trip. `Navigate { url: Some(_) }` resolves its URL from the event arena
   / batch string section (same dual convention as `TEXT_CHANGED`);
   `Navigate { url: None }` is a native back request (decodes from a bare
   opcode).
 - **`Guest::set_date`** helper (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`).
 - **`Guest::set_design_token`** helper (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`): global token
   override (`path` arena string, `valueType`, `value`), incl. `dark.`-prefixed
   dark variants (spec/TOKENS.md).
 - **`Guest::set_design_token_string`** helper: STRING-valued token override —
   both the path and the value ride the arena (`A` = path ref, `B` = STRING,
   `C` = value ref).
 - **`Guest::set_color_scheme` / `Guest::reset_theme`** helpers
   (`META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` / `META::RESET_THEME`): force the renderer color
   scheme (platform/light/dark) and clear all application token overrides.
 - **`pathland_core::tokens`** — the **reference resolution algorithm**
   (spec/TOKENS.md): `dark.*` layer → override → default → parent-fallback →
   fallback, the generative `space.<N>` family (`space.base` × N), and the
   `TokenValue`/`Scheme`/`TokenTables` types. Pure `no_std` + `alloc`;
   renderers keep their own tables and call `tokens::resolve`. `resolve_ref`
   implements explicit `dark.` references (forced dark layer regardless of the
   active scheme). `TIER1_TOKENS` is the canonical Tier-1 catalog used by the
   renderer default-table coverage tests. The full "Design-Token Resolution
   Conformance" table (spec/CONFORMANCE.md) is tested here.
 - **`value_type_for`** matches `spec/MODIFIERS.md`'s canonical mapping
   (COLOR / U32 / U8 / STRING / F32-enum-code / LIST); the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value
   type (`0x08`) is available per-instance on `SET_PROPERTY`. **`LIST`** (`0x09`)
   is the arena-backed array value type (a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
 - **`SizeThatFits`** (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` `0x17`, `FIT_QUERY` `0x1039` LIST,
   `FIT_CHANGED` `0x13`): the fit slot shows its single selected child (only it
   is transmitted); `fit::fit_index` implements the spec'd pick (largest
   threshold the width meets, ascending + stable, index 0 fallback) shared by
   every renderer.
 - **Listener bits**: 0–9 (`POINTER_*`, `KEY_*`, `FOCUS`, `EDITING`, `SUBMIT`,
   `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`).
 - **`SCROLL_AXIS`** (`0x0021`, F32 enum: `Vertical`=0 default, `Horizontal`=1):
   a `SCROLLVIEW`'s scroll axis. The view is greedy on this axis; the cross axis
   hugs its content (fill propagation) — spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ScrollView.
 - **`constants::role`** — the canonical **`ROLE` semantic-structure catalog**
   (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties), **renumbered dense** (0–13): `HEADER`
   (heading), `PARAGRAPH`, `LIST`, `LIST_ITEM`, `SUMMARY`, `BANNER`,
   `NAVIGATION`, `MAIN`, `CONTENT_INFO`, `COMPLEMENTARY`, `ARTICLE`, `SECTION`,
   `SEARCH`. Interactive/control roles are **not roles** — they are intrinsic to
   the control components; the DSL rejects codes outside this catalog. Single
   source the renderers, DSLs, and `pathland-ts-codegen` bind to.
 - **`constants::text_style`** — the canonical **`TEXT_STYLE` predefined
   typographies** (spec/MODIFIERS.md): `LARGE_TITLE`…`HEADLINE` (heading styles →
   `<h1>`–`<h5>` on a `TEXT`), plus `SUBHEADLINE`/`BODY`/`CALLOUT`/`FOOTNOTE`/
   `CAPTION`/`CAPTION2` (plain `<span>` text). `TEXT_STYLE = 0x1032`.
 - **Shared linear memory**: 80-byte header, guest→host ring, host→guest event
   ring, guest arena, host→guest **event arena** (two-way string section — a
   host `send_event(TextChanged)` round-trips text over the shared ring).
 - **Wrap-safe ring reads (both directions)**: the masked write cursor can lap
   the read cursor numerically (the producer wraps through 0), and the naive
   `write < read` guard in `read_events` / `Host::frames` **permanently
   deadlocked the ring** at the wrap boundary — the reader never advanced again,
   the writer sat "full", and every subsequent drain returned empty (the GTK
   demo's "UI freezes some time into a song, audio keeps playing": events were
   written but `drain_events` returned 0 forever). Both readers now count the
   pending run modulo the ring size and drain across the wrap in ring order
   (`Host::frames` drains the wrapped head in one call and the tail in the next,
   preserving opcode order). Event drains also take a `max` bound
   (`drain_event_opcodes_max`) so a fixed-size C buffer never drops events it
   could not copy. Regression tests: `ring::tests::read_events_drains_a_wrapped_producer`
   + `tests::host_frames_survives_a_wrapped_write_cursor`.
 - **Conformance vectors** (`conformance.rs`): TREE/PARAMETER/META/EVENT golden
   bytes **incl. vectors 17–18, 20–27** (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (COLOR +
   STRING-valued), `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY`, `NAVIGATE`±URL,
   `ROUTE`, `TRANSITION`, `META::ENVIRONMENT` VIEWPORT_WIDTH + ROUTE), vectors
   **34–38** (grid `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`/`GRID_TRACKS`, `GRID_ROW`,
   `ALIGNMENT` topCenter, `PROXY_VIEW`), and the network-only **`META::PING`/`PONG`** heartbeat
   opcodes; a ring
   test proving `Guest::set_design_token` emits vector 17 byte-exactly;
   `cargo test` enforces them.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - `ENVIRONMENT` (`META`) is a constant + the field-id family; the **string
   codec over the shared ring** (event-arena absolute offset for a `ROUTE`
   field) and a native emitter are not wired yet — the web path encodes/decodes
   it in the TS client + Java `FrameCodec` (batch string section).
 - Enum *value* codes (e.g. `TOGGLE_STYLE=Switch=0`) are used inline; there are
   no named value constants. (`ROLE` and `TEXT_STYLE` are now the canonical
   exceptions — see `constants::role` / `constants::text_style` above; the
   remaining enum codes live in the specs + the `pathland-ts-codegen` enum
   table.)
 - No **general STRING-property diff path** in `pathland-engine` (the engine
   stores numeric properties + design-token refs only). `ROUTE` (STRING) will
   need a small string-property capability when the Rust router lands (Phase 3);
   `TRANSITION` (F32) is handled by the generic property diff today.
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `ITEM_COUNT` (0x0022),
+  `ITEM_EXTENT` (0x0023), `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` (0x0024), the `VISIBLE_RANGE`
+  event (0x15), and listener bit 10 are specified but not in `constants` yet.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-core` — conformance vectors, opcode round-trips,
 arena, ring, event-ring (incl. shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` + `Navigate` round
 trips and `META::RESET` event-arena recycle), `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` /

 refs), randomized tests.

 **Last updated:** November 12, 2026
 
 The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
 diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes. Protocol contract:
 `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Attributed text**: `Node::attributed_text` + `attributed_binding` emit
   `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` instead of `SET_TEXT`; the snapshot stores the
   encoded value plus its arena offset, so an unchanged payload emits zero
   opcodes and a changed signal re-emits only the bound node. Switching back to
   plain text re-emits `SET_TEXT`.
 - **Auto-parsed Markdown**: `Node::markdown_text` parses static text and string
   signals through the shared `pathland-markdown` crate. The raw source is stored
   in the snapshot so unchanged text emits zero opcodes; plain results use the
   compact `SET_TEXT` path and only rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
 - **Window metadata bindings**: `Engine::bind_window_metadata`/`bind_window_field` bind fields to signals; mount emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields, a signal write emits only the changed field, and unchanged values emit zero opcodes.

   `string_properties`, `token_properties`, text/property signal bindings,
   app-side gestures). Components include `Icon` (→ `component_type::ICON`).
 - **String-valued properties**: `Node::string_properties` (property → value,
   e.g. `FONT_FAMILY`, `LABEL`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the
   `STRING` value type (arena-allocated); unchanged strings reuse their arena
   offset — steady-state emission stays zero-alloc with string props present
   (proven by test).
 - **Components** (`Component` enum): the full spec set — `VStack`, `HStack`,
   `ZStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`,
   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`,
   `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` — all mapped to
   `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
 - **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
   property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
 - **Design-token property refs**: `Node::token_properties` (property → token
   path) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; unchanged
   refs reuse their arena offset across passes — **steady-state emission stays
   zero-alloc with token refs present** (proven by test).
 - **`Engine::set_design_token`** — emits a global `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
   override (base or `dark.`-prefixed) into the current frame.
 - **Global theme overrides** (`theme.rs`): `Theme` — single-value builders
   (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme { light,
   dark }` composes a light + dark pair. `Engine::apply_theme` (light-only) and
   `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light as base, dark with the `dark.` prefix;
   STRING values arena-alloc'd) emit the overrides once at mount — they never
   re-emit nodes.
 - **Runtime theming** (`Engine::reset_theme`, `Engine::set_color_scheme`,
   `Engine::replace_theme`, `Engine::replace_adaptive_theme`): emits
   `META::RESET_THEME` / `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`; `ColorSchemeMode`
   (`Platform`/`Light`/`Dark`) mirrors the wire modes. Replacement is
   reset + apply in one frame; no tree node is re-emitted.
 - **Shared engine traces**: `pathland-engine-golden` emits self-contained
   PLPL frames for mount and signal-delta scenarios under `spec/engine-traces/`;
   the JVM `EngineTraceTest` compares byte-for-byte. The canonical mount order is
   documented in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Reactive runtime** (`signal.rs`): a shared `Runtime`
   (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; the "current computation"
   is an explicit stack in the store) owns value signals, **computed** signals
   (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and **effects** (run
   immediately, then on dependency change) plus `untracked` reads. Typed handles
   `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (`SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`);
   `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. Node text/properties bound
   to a signal re-emit only the bound node on change — including a computed's
   bound nodes (`set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps).
 - **Signals bound to node text/properties**: `set_signal` re-emits only the
   bound nodes (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`); `get_signal` returns the current value.
 - **Gestures / input sinks**: `Gesture::Tap` (app-side callback) plus the
   two-way binding sinks `Gesture::ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` (with
   `TapHandler`/`ValueInputHandler`/`TextInputHandler`/`DateInputHandler` aliases).
   `collect_tap_handlers` and `collect_input_handlers` (→ `InputHandlers`) expose
   the app-side registries; sinks are never serialized.
 - **Media controller** (`media.rs`, spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the
   app-side state object owning a resource (`source`/`bind_source`) and its
   transport as signals: commands `playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/
   `looping`/`rate` (each rebindable to an app-owned signal), report feeds
   `time`/`duration`/`volume_report`, `on_ended`, and the convenience transport
   (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`set_volume`/`set_muted`/`set_looping`/
   `set_rate`). A node references one through the identity-compared
   `MediaControllerRef` (`Node.media_controller`); `Component::MediaController`
   (0x30, non-visual) is the controller's node and `Component::Video` is its
   surface. **Audio has no view.**
 - **String property bindings** (`Node.string_bindings`): a `STRING`-valued
   property bound to a signal (e.g. a controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) re-emits only
   that property (`SET_PROPERTY`, `STRING`, arena-allocated) on change — a track
   change emits exactly one opcode.
 - **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids) — the **single id authority**: it hands
   out unique ids, satisfying the frame's **unique-node-id invariant**
   (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle — a frame never carries two nodes with the same
   id). **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
   was first given, so a structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the
   playback key; the same pass links each `VIDEO` surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`
   to the controller node.

   `VIDEO` unbound when its new controller marker comes later in tree order.
   Controller-first layouts work; order independence is not yet satisfied. See
   the [reproduction and proposed fix](../../../../docs/audits/media-controller-identity.md#media-001--rust-surface-first-binding-is-absent-on-initial-assignment).
 - Only the `Tap` gesture plus value/text/date input sinks; no other gesture.
 - Signal-bound properties cannot carry token refs (a token ref is a static path).
 - `get_signal` returns an owned value (the store is shared via `Rc<RefCell>`).
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: no `ForEach` data source, window
+  signal, keyed window reconcile, or `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/

 `cargo test -p pathland-engine` — emitter deltas, signals (values, computed,
 effects, `untracked`), `component_type_id`.

 # pathland-render-core — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **toolkit-free renderer core shared by every Pathland renderer** (GTK4, Qt,
 …): opcode-frame decode into a retained native-element description
 (`RenderTree` / `HostNode`) plus the design-token resolution contract
 (spec/TOKENS.md). Protocol contract: `spec/`. This crate touches **no toolkit**
 (no GTK, no Qt) — it is pure protocol + tokens.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata decode**: `RenderTree` stores `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (`WindowMeta`), shared by the GTK/Qt renderers; empty strings clear fields.
 
 - **`RenderTree` / `HostNode`** (extracted from `pathland-render-gtk`'s
   `host.rs`, which was already GTK-free):
   - `TREE` ops → node tree: `CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
     `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD` (append/insert at `u32::MAX`), parent/child
     bookkeeping.
   - `STYLE` ops → node properties: `SET_PROPERTY` (numeric `properties`,
     `STRING` resolved from the arena into `strings`, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs kept
     in `token_refs`), `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (global overrides, base +
     `dark.` split), and `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (decoded into
     `HostNode::attributed`, with the plain `text` fallback populated).
   - Node accessors: `node(id)`, `root()`, string/f32/u32 property helpers,
     `checked()`.
 - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
   - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides stored (base + `dark.*` by path
     prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolved from the arena).
   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path and
     **resolve at apply time** against the theme, the active scheme, and the
     parent-fallback chain into concrete `properties`/`strings`
     (`resolve_tokens`, reusing `pathland_core::tokens::resolve_ref`); paths
     are kept for re-resolution on scheme change.
   - Explicit `dark.` references resolve the dark layer in either scheme.
   - Previously materialized token values are removed before each resolution,
     so an unresolvable reference (or a reset override) leaves the property
     unset instead of retaining a stale value. A literal `SET_PROPERTY`
     replaces a previous token reference (and vice versa).
   - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) via `concrete_default_tables` —
     concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks; a renderer may enrich with native
     theme colors via `RenderTree::set_defaults`.
   - Platform scheme (`set_scheme`) and application override
     (`set_scheme_override(Option<Scheme>)`, `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) are
     separate; the effective scheme is the override when set.
   - `reset_theme()` / `META::RESET_THEME` clears base + `dark.*` overrides and
     re-resolves against renderer defaults.
   - `concrete_default_tables` now covers the full `TIER1_TOKENS` catalog in
     both schemes (coverage-tested).
 - **`render_tree_from_frame`** — decode a fresh tree from one frame.
 - **`describe`** — one-opcode human-readable line (debugging aid).
 
 ## Consumed by
 
 - `pathland-render-gtk` (decode + token resolution; the GTK-specific
   `tokens.rs` GTK theme-color enrichment stays in that crate).
 - `pathland-render-qt` (planned).
 - `pathland-view-native` and `pathland-core-transport` dev-tests (decode a
   frame into a `RenderTree` without pulling in a toolkit).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - No layout computation (by design — the protocol never emits rects).
 - No META handling beyond theming (`SET_COLOR_SCHEME`/`RESET_THEME`); `RESET` /
   `ENVIRONMENT` / `RESYNC` remain renderer-owned concerns.
 - Web renderers do not yet implement the parent-path fallback (`font.body` →
   `font.body.size`) in CSS; native renderers do via the shared resolver.
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/
+  `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` are not decoded into `HostNode` yet.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-render-core` — decode of a declarative frame (no
 layout/rect data present), delta-frame application (unchanged nodes preserved),
 and STRING property resolution from the arena. Full decode/token coverage also
 runs through `pathland-render-gtk`'s tests (`cargo test`).

   image now decodes and scales the content into the box (via gdk-pixbuf), making

   `AdwNavigationView` is only the renderer's rendered-output cache.

   appearing/disappearing (e.g. a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap) never restarts the

   `PLAYBACK_STATE` → pipeline `Playing`/`Paused`, `MEDIA_POSITION` → seek

   stream advances (which caused the position to skip back periodically). A changed

   through the shared event sink/ring, **targeting the controller id**:

     straight onto the playbin, and rate is applied as a **rate-seeking seek** from
     the current position (GStreamer has no standalone rate setter). Every later
     seek re-applies the rate, so a `MEDIA_RATE` is not silently reset by a seek;
     rate ≤ 0 (reverse) is ignored — not a transport control Pathland models.
   - **Verified from the DSL**: a test builds the Rust DSL's `MediaController` +

     asserting the non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node carries `MEDIA_SOURCE` +

     controller maps to no widget (`WidgetKind::Invisible`). (A runnable demo
     section still needs a bundled asset — the Java GTK demo covers that path.)

     `pathland-media-<id>` thread that performs *every* GStreamer operation —
     state changes, FLUSH seeks, `query_position`, and the bus drain — so the GTK

     some time into a song, audio keeps playing" class of bug). The main thread
     sends non-blocking control messages (`Play`/`Seek`/`Volume`/`Stop`) and a

     logic (`should_report_time`, the post-seek suppression window set when the
     worker reports `SeekApplied`) before the sink sees them.

     the pump (`RefCell already borrowed`) and panicking. Such events are now

   NOT implemented in the GTK renderer (removed)** — a fit slot node is unmapped (no
   widget), `FIT_QUERY` is not decoded, and no `FIT_CHANGED` is reported. The protocol,
   core, Java DSL, Rust DSL/engine, web (SSR + DOM) and server-routing surfaces are
   implemented; GTK rendering is deferred because **GTK4 has no size-change
   notification** (the GTK3 `size-allocate` signal was removed; there is no CSS
   `@container` analog) — a future renderer would observe its own allocation via a
   frame-clock `add_tick_callback` (or a `GtkWidget` `allocate` override), derive the
   fit with `pathland_core::fit::fit_index`, and report `FIT_CHANGED` only on band
   crossings.

   rule on **both** axes (main axis: only `FILL`/greedy children stretch and
   leftover goes to them, everything else positioned at the start; cross axis:
   only `FILL`/greedy children stretch, otherwise positioned by `ALIGNMENT`
   defaulting to Leading), grid cells apply the same rule, and the greedy
   primitives (`DIVIDER` cross-axis, `SPACER` main-axis, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW`
   both) fill by nature. The old composite-button main-axis hack was retired
   (superseded by the parent stack's rule). Conformance C1–C6 covered by the
   pure decision tests in `layout.rs`.

   `hexpand`/`vexpand` is set from the same effective-`FILL` decision as its
   alignment, so a Hug main-axis child (`valign=Start`, `vexpand=false`) can
   never claim leftover — a `GtkBox` otherwise hands extra space to children
   left at GTK's default `Align::Fill`, which spread e.g. a library's rows
   vertically instead of pinning them to the leading edge (the trailing
   `SPACER` absorbs the leftover). This also makes `SPACER` cross-axis
   non-expanding.

   `effective_fill` in `layout.rs` resolves a Hug-sized stack/ZStack that
   contains a `FILL` child / `Spacer` / greedy primitive on an axis as `FILL` on
   that axis (SwiftUI/Compose parity), so it fills its parent's proposal.
   Covered by `fill_propagates_through_a_hug_stack`.
 - **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — every child is an overlay
   (later = on top) that keeps its own size unless effectively `FILL`, positioned
   by the ZStack `ALIGNMENT` on **both** axes (`sync_overlay_children`); the
   overlay hugs to its largest child; fill propagation applies. The old
   first-child-pinned-to-fill `GtkOverlay` main-child behavior is gone.

   folded into the margins by `apply_padding` as the **lowest-precedence base**

   layout model) and no longer applied in `apply_style` (where it previously
   overrode the higher-precedence `PADDING`). Matches the HTML renderer.
   Covered by `content_margins_are_the_lowest_precedence_base`.

   re-set every frame), on **grids** (`row_spacing`/`column_spacing` from
   `SPACING`, `sync_grid_children`), and on **composite-control bodies**
   (`sync_composite_children` reads the control node's `SPACING` — a control
   whose label flattened a stack, e.g. `Button.of(HStack, …)`, carries the
   stack's `SPACING`, and its body box reproduces the gap like the HTML
   renderer's `gap`). Covered by `spacing_clamps_and_rounds_for_any_node`.

   `set_overflow(Overflow::Hidden)` (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity, spec LAYOUT.md /
   PRIMITIVES.md: a Fixed box constrains layout but only clips when set).

   wraps the label within the box (`set_wrap` + `WordChar`); `LINE_LIMIT` clamps

   fidelity: `ellipsize_from` maps Head/Middle/Tail → `EllipsizeMode::Start/
   Middle/End` — reliable for single-line labels, best-effort on a multi-line
   clamp.

   request — GTK has no max-size API, so a widget whose natural size exceeds its
   Fixed box (e.g. a stack wider than its box) is allocated its natural size
   rather than clipped to the box. Text wraps within its box (above) and
   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips overflow; other content may still exceed a Fixed box.

Non-JVM hosts that embed the cdylib must refresh it with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` (not just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the shared library). The JVM no longer embeds it; `GoldenConformanceTest` guards the Java port against golden-fixture drift. - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors, strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`). ## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift) The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated (`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the contract both renderers must satisfy. ## Not implemented / gaps - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (spec/LAYOUT.md §content fitting): aligned — it **alone** has no observable effect (the old `nowrap`+`text-overflow:ellipsis` emission is gone, SSR + TS DOM client); under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp the renderer tail- ellipsizes via `line-clamp`. Renderer-owned fidelity: CSS cannot place a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to the tail ellipsis. - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding/content margins, corner radius, opacity, width/height, border width/color, shadow color/x/y/radius). **Parent-path fallback and per-component native control chrome are not implemented in CSS** (see the gaps above). - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**: grids emit `gap` from `SPACING`, equal-`1fr` track templates from the `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/ LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/ `minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, taking precedence over the count), and **per-cell alignment** — each cell is wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell, else the grid `ALIGNMENT` position (default start) — with `justify-items`/ `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy on its `SCROLL_AXIS` only, carries `data-pathland-scroll-axis`, and renders **only its first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C20 covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. `gridrow`, `scrollaxis`, and `maxbounds`). +- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/ + `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` virtual extent, window placement, and the first-window SSR + form are not implemented; lazy stacks render as plain flex with all emitted + children. C21–C24 are not covered yet. - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property). - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact. - **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web. - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — no external/webfont loading, so the rendered document makes no network requests for fonts and works offline. An app can still pick its own typeface via a `font.body.family` `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override (any STRING value, e.g. `"Inter"` if the app hosts it). - Compound token refs cover shadow x/y/radius and border width (the DOM client mirrors them); per-component tokens still style only the component CSS the renderer owns. ## Verified by `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 77 headless render tests (components, properties, composite, event attrs, navigation slot route/transition attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames, inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). The built-in CSS tests assert the generated bundle is embedded (reset, tokens, component rules) and that component rules reference the catalog/metadata tokens; the linked-mode tests assert the hashed `<link>` and that the default render remains inline. `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard. `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check` and `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` validate the design pipeline and the committed bundle.

 # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
 scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
 - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata**: a changed `TITLE` is forwarded to the Qt layer as `PLQT_SET_WINDOW_TITLE`; unchanged metadata emits zero commands.
 
 - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
 - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
 - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
 - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
   `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
   padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
   `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item` (children share one box, positioned by the 2D
   `ALIGNMENT` code on both axes, re-derived on resize; the Hug stack's own size
   is the **max child** per axis, and an "effectively FILL" child — explicit
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, a greedy primitive, or fill propagation through a
   nested stack/Spacers — stretches to the box), `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView`
   (content attaches to its `contentItem`; **greedy on its `SCROLL_AXIS`**
   (vertical by default), the **cross axis hugs its content** and fill-propagates
   (a `FILL`-width content child makes the viewport full-width); content is
   **unbounded on the scroll axis** (keeps its natural size and may grow beyond
   the viewport) and **bounded to the viewport on the cross axis**; an explicit
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides greed and `HUG_CONTENT` sizes the viewport to the
   content), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR` → `Rectangle`, `SHAPE` →
   `Rectangle` with `SHAPE_KIND` geometry (Circle/Capsule/Ellipse round to
   `min(w,h)/2` — Ellipse is a uniform-radius approximation; Rectangle is
   square-cornered; RoundedRectangle keeps `BORDER_RADIUS`; `Path` unsupported),
   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`, **padding** (`PADDING_*` > `PADDING`
   > `CONTENT_MARGINS`, order-independent — stacks get real inner padding whose
   per-edge values also feed the hugged implicit size; non-stack leaves get
   margins — `Layout.*Margin` inside a layout, `anchors.*Margin` for roots/anchored
   leaves. Gap: a leaf positioned by ZStack alignment (no anchors) isn't inset),
   width/height (`-1`
   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family/style via the `font`
   `QFont` property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible,
   z, value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode` = `TextInput.Password` (masked), progress/indeterminate,
   selection→currentIndex, prompt/label→placeholder, image source.
   **`OFFSET_X`/`OFFSET_Y`** are a post-layout QML `Translate` transform (composes
   with layout/alignment instead of being overwritten). **`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`**
   disables the item's mouse acceptance and any attached pointer MouseArea without
   hiding it. **Stack alignment**: a stack's `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on
   the cross axis via
   its `Layout` attached properties (Start/Center/End; `Fill`(3)/absent = default
   HUG/start, never a stretch — spec/LAYOUT.md).
   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
 - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
 - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
   `DELETE`.
 - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
 - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
   init.
 - **Design tokens / theming**: `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides and
   `DESIGN_TOKEN` property references are decoded by the shared
   `pathland-render-core` tree and diffed to QML like any other property;
   `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces platform/light/dark (the platform signal is
   stored but ignored while forced) and `META::RESET_THEME` clears app
   overrides. Explicit `dark.` references and unknown-token fallback follow the
   shared resolver. Qt-specific defaults are the shared concrete Tier-1 tables
   (no `QPalette` enrichment yet).
 - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
 - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
 - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
   sets it before `runRing`.
 - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
   a bare program name to Qt.
 - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
   overflowing title).
 
 - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
     (spec/MEDIA.md).
   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
     parent/child edge).
   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
     fills it.
   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
     the parent Grid.
 - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width; equal thresholds keep the lower index; empty
   table → 0) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` once after the first measure, then only
   when the index changes. The report is a layout result, not a value echo, so
   it is not suppressed while a frame's properties are applied. The slot shows
   exactly one selected child, which fills the slot.
 - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
 - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
 - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
     native.
   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
   - **Layout defaults (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: the cross axis **hugs** by default
     (never CSS `align-items:stretch`); only an *effectively FILL* child stretches
     — explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, a layout-greedy primitive (`SPACER` main,
     `DIVIDER` cross, `COLOR`/`SIZE_THAT_FITS` both, `SCROLLVIEW` its
     `SCROLL_AXIS` only), or **fill
     propagation** (a Hug stack/ZStack/proxy whose subtree carries a FILL
     child/greedy filler). An explicit fixed size **or `HUG_CONTENT`**
     (`PL_SIZE_HUG`) overrides a primitive's natural greed. `ALIGNMENT` only
     positions (`Fill(3)` = default hug).
     Recomputed at each frame boundary (`recomputeLayout`), so `RESET_NODE`'s
     style reset can't wipe it. Plus `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
     offset shadow layer.
 - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
   echo-suppressed). `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` is reported **only on a media
   error** (`InvalidMedia`), never for app-driven play/pause or the natural end —
   matching the DOM client (reports play/pause only with native controls) and GTK
   (error only). There are no renderer-native audio controls, so a play-state echo
   would otherwise write the app's `PLAYBACK_STATE` command to pause and stop the
   next track (advanced on `MEDIA_ENDED`) from playing. A play/pause declared
   before the source is re-applied when the source lands.
   **Idempotent transport**: `MEDIA_SOURCE` reloads only when the resolved
   resource changes and `MEDIA_POSITION` seeks only when the command target
   changes, so the diff's full-property re-send (e.g. a volume drag on the
   controller) never restarts the stream or jumps to a stale position — mirrors
   `pathland-render-gtk`.
 - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/MAX_*`
   (`IDEAL_*` retired),
   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
   where applicable).
 - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **Rich text (`SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`)**: deferred; the Qt renderer uses the
   payload's plain `HostNode.text` fallback (runs/links are not styled yet).
 - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
 - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
   dialog.
 - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
   Per-component design tokens (`button.*`, `toggle.*`, `slider.*`, …) are
   therefore not applied to native leaf chrome automatically — an app can still
   emit explicit token-referenced properties.
 - **Qt-native token defaults**: no `QPalette` → Tier-1 default enrichment yet;
   the renderer uses the shared concrete fallback table.
 - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
 - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
   `MultiEffect` shadow.
 - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
   `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
   listener mask bit).
 - **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
   `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
   defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
   `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
 - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
 - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
   the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH (exercised by the nav adapter tests).
 - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).

 # pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
 Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata constants**: `CMD_SET_WINDOW_METADATA` + `WINDOW_TITLE/DESCRIPTION/LOCALE` are generated from `pathland_core`.
 - **Attributed text**: `CMD_SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` is generated from
   `pathland_core::parameter`.
 
 - **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
   bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
   revalue changes the emitted file); the protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
   shape kind, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/` — `ROLE_*` is bound to
   `pathland_core::constants::role` (the semantic-only catalog, dense 0–13) and
   `TEXT_STYLE_*` to `pathland_core::constants::text_style`.
 - **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
   the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `tokenToForcedDarkCssVar`,
   `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables)
   emitted from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust
   renderer and the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it. Explicit
   `dark.` references resolve to `--pl-dark-…` and plain refs carry the
   `unset` fallback.
 - **`generated/role-spec.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/role-spec.ts`):
   the semantic `ROLE` → element + typography → heading conventions emitted from
   `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — `ROLE_TAGS`, `HEADING_STYLES`,
   `ShellKind`, and the `semanticTag`/`textTag`/`ariaRole`/`headingLevel`
   resolvers — so semantic-tag / ARIA / heading decisions cannot drift between
   the Rust SSR renderer and the DOM client. `constants.ts` also carries the
   media surface (`COMPONENT_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`/`VIDEO`, `PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE`/
   `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_*` event commands) and the icon surface (`COMPONENT_ICON`,
   `PROP_ICON_NAME`).
 - **Icon glyph map — intentionally NOT generated.** The full canonical icon
   catalog (`generated/icons.ts`, ~13KB in the bundle) was **removed**: the DOM
   client no longer carries glyph data. SSR inlines only the icons the page uses,
   and a runtime swap to a name the page did not embed lazily fetches
   `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the host — which serves it from the shared
   Rust renderer (`pathland_html_icon_svg`, the same `pathland-render-html::icons`
   source SSR inlines from), so glyph parity between SSR and the client is
   guaranteed by the single Rust source, not by a mirrored TS map.
 - **`npm run regen`** (`lib/typescript/scripts/regen.mjs`) runs both generators
   (and the golden-fixture emitter); CI's `rust` job runs them and fails on
   `git diff --exit-code` drift.
 
 ## Regenerate
 
 `npm run regen` (from `lib/typescript`) or `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`
 (from `lib/rust`), then commit the generated files with the change that produced
 them.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - Theme/scheme **runtime** behavior is handled by `apply.ts` + `tokens.ts`,
   not generated. Only the pure-data surfaces are generated. The element-shell factory
   (`elements.ts`) and the property-handler table (`classes.ts`) are still
   hand-written — their alignment is enforced behaviorally by the
   `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness rather than generated. Extending
-  the generator to those tables is the planned next step.

 # pathland-view-native — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** August 28, 2026
 
 The **native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`**: a flat world over the shared-memory
 ring for foreign hosts (Swift/Java via FFI). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata C ABI**: `pathland_native_window_metadata(host, field, signal)` binds a field to a string signal (title/description/locale), re-emitting only the changed field.
 
 - **`NativeHost`**: owns the shared ring, `create_node`/`set_property`/
   `set_text`, frame emission, `drain_events`.
 - **Component mapping** (`component_from_id`/`component_id`): the full
   component set — stacks, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, and all drawing/
   container/semantic-control components, using the renumbered ids.
 - **Property value types** (`property_value_type`): COLOR (incl.
   `COLOR_VALUE`/`COLOR_MULTIPLY`/`SHADOW_COLOR`), U32 (`EVENT_LISTENERS`/
   `BORDER_EDGES`/`ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`LINE_LIMIT`/`SELECTION`), STRING
   (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE`), U8 (`VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/
   `SELECTED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`/`UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`/`COLOR_INVERT`/
   `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`/`IS_SECURE`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`/`FIXED_SIZE_*`), else F32.
 - **Signals** C ABI (`signal_*`, `node_bind_text`/`node_bind_property`/
   `node_bind_string_property`).
 - **Media C ABI** (`media_controller_create`/`_signal`/`_source`,
   `node_media_controller`) — spec/MEDIA.md.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - STRING-valued properties are typed as STRING but the flat world has no
   arena-alloc helper to emit them (callers must `pathland_core_arena_alloc`).
 - **Media**: `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`/`VIDEO` are mapped in `component_from_id`/
   `component_id`, and the flat world **authors media**: `media_controller_create`
   returns a handle (the controller is an engine-side `Rc` held by the host),
   `media_controller_signal(handle, slot)` addresses each transport slot (driven
   with `signal_set_*`), `media_controller_source` sets a static resource;
   `node_media_controller(node, handle)` makes a node the controller's own
   `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node or one of its `VIDEO` surfaces, and the generic
   `node_bind_string_property` binds a reactive `MEDIA_SOURCE`. Materialization
   links each surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` to the controller's host-supplied
   node id. (Hosts that supply ids themselves need no pinning.)
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: no flat API for a `ForEach` data
+  source, window signal, or `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/`FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`
+  emission.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-view-native` — flat-world emission, component mapping,
 signal deltas.
