 ## B. Layout & Container Primitives
 
 Layout primitives arrange children. They carry `SPACING` (0x0001),
 `ALIGNMENT` (0x0002), and `CONTENT_MARGINS` (0x0005), plus layout modifiers from
 [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#1-layout). Renderers map them to their native
 layout primitives.
 
 ### The stack layout model
 
 `VStack`/`HStack` (and the lazy stacks) follow the **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose
 layout model**: a stack *proposes* a size to each child, the child reports its
 own size, and the stack *places* it. The protocol transmits **intent** — size
 kinds and alignment — never geometry; the renderer resolves the proposal with
 its native layout engine. The full allocation contract is
 [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md); the essentials:
 
 **Size kinds.** Each `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` is one of three kinds (LAYOUT.md §size
 model):
 
 | Kind | Wire value | Meaning |
 |------|-----------|---------|
 | **Fixed** | finite `F32` | exactly that many points |
 | **Fill** | `-1` | expand to available space |
 | **Hug** | `-2` / absent | natural size |
 
 **Main vs cross axis.** The **main axis** is the stack's layout direction
 (VStack = vertical, HStack = horizontal); the other is the **cross axis**.
 
 **Main-axis allocation.** A child is Fixed (exact box), Fill (expands), or Hug
 (natural). **Leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill` children** (and to
 `Spacer`, which is Fill by nature); a stack with no Fill child leaves the
 leftover empty at the end. Every other child is packed from the start.
 
 **Cross-axis allocation.** A child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
 **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` — position-only, it never resizes. A stack reads a
 **single axis** of the 2D position code (see the [ZStack alignment
 table](#zstack--zstack-0x12)): a `VStack` reads the horizontal component
 (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), an `HStack` the vertical (`0/1/2` =
 top/center/bottom). The default is the start position (Compose `Column` defaults
 `Alignment.Start`, `Row` defaults `Alignment.Top`; SwiftUI's stack default is
 `.center` — a per-framework difference, all three are expressible with an
 explicit `ALIGNMENT`). Only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's
 cross size.
 
 **Fill propagation.** A Hug-sized stack that contains a **`Fill`-sized child or
 `Spacer` on an axis is itself `Fill`-sized on that axis** — the child's
 expansion propagates to the stack, which then fills its parent's proposal on
 that axis. This matches both reference frameworks:
 
 - SwiftUI `VStack { Button().frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }` fills the width.
 - Compose `Column { Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) }` fills the width.
 - `VStack { Spacer() }` fills the proposed height.
 
 A full-width row is therefore expressed as a `Fill`-width child (or `Spacer`)
 inside the stack, never by stretching the stack itself.
 
 **Spacing.** `SPACING` is a fixed gap between **adjacent** children (never
 before the first or after the last), clamped to ≥ 0. It matches SwiftUI
 `VStack(spacing:)` and Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`. Leftover space is
 distributed by `Fill` children / `Spacer`, never by the gap.
 
 **Insets.** `CONTENT_MARGINS` is the stack's uniform content inset
 (equivalently, `PADDING` on the stack). Both compose; when both are present on
 the same node, precedence is per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` >
 `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
 
 **Overflow.** A Fixed box **constrains layout but does not clip**: content that
 exceeds the box is drawn outside it unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI
 `.clipped()` parity). A stack inside a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.
 
 ### VStack — `VSTACK` 0x10
 
 Vertical flex stack. **Properties**: `SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT` (enum: `Leading`=0,
 `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
 
 **Layout & sizing**
 
 - **Main axis (vertical)**: children are allocated per the stack model —
   Fixed exact, Fill expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A
   Hug VStack's height is the sum of its children's heights plus `SPACING`
   between them.
 - **Cross axis (horizontal)**: children keep their own width (a Fixed box, or a
   Hug natural width); `Fill`-width children stretch to the stack's width. Narrow
   children are positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default Leading/Start).
 - **Own size**: Hug by default (height = content + spacing; width = widest
   child). A Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
   propagation — expands to the parent's proposal. A `Fill`-width child makes
   the stack full-width; a `Fill`-height child makes it full-height.
 - **Edge cases**: negative `SPACING` → 0; no Fill child + leftover → empty at
   the end; a Fixed-width child narrower than the stack keeps its exact box and
   is aligned; a `Fill` child in a Hug stack propagates (fills the parent's
   proposal); root stacks are typically `Fill`
   (`.modifiers(frame(f -> f.width(FILL).height(FILL)))`).
 
 ### HStack — `HSTACK` 0x11
 
 Horizontal flex stack. Same properties as `VStack`, mirrored:
 
 - **Main axis (horizontal)**: children per the stack model — Fixed exact, Fill
   expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A Hug HStack's width
   is the sum of its children's widths plus `SPACING`.
 - **Cross axis (vertical)**: children keep their own height (Fixed or Hug);
   `Fill`-height children stretch. Positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default
   Leading/Start; Compose `Row` defaults to `Top`, SwiftUI's HStack to `.center`).
 - **Own size**: Hug by default (width = content + spacing; height = tallest
   child); a Fixed box exact; `Fill`/propagation expands.
 - **Edge cases**: as VStack.
 
 ### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12
 
 Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
 draw order**, later = on top. An explicit `Z_INDEX` overrides that order: a
 higher value draws **on top of** lower values, and equal values tie-break by
 child index (SwiftUI `.zIndex(_:)` parity). **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum:
 `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill
 `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `PADDING`, `CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset). **No `SPACING`** —
 children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.
 
 **Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)
 
 - **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
   other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
   Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
   **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
 - **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
   axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
   Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
   propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
   axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.
   `ZStack { Color.red }` fills (Color is layout-greedy); `ZStack { Text("hi") }`
   hugs the text.
 - **Alignment**: `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on **both** axes with a
   **2D position code** (SwiftUI `Alignment` / Compose `Alignment` parity) — the
   code's horizontal and vertical components place the child within the stack's
   box. Position-only: it never resizes a child.
 
   | code | horizontal | vertical | meaning |
   |------|------------|----------|---------|
   | `0` | start | start | top-leading |
   | `1` | center | center | centered |
   | `2` | end | end | bottom-trailing |
   | `3` | center | start | top-center |
   | `4` | center | end | bottom-center |
   | `5` | start | center | center-leading |
   | `6` | end | center | center-trailing |
   | `7` | end | start | top-trailing |
   | `8` | start | end | bottom-leading |
 
   `0`/absent is the default (top-leading, Compose `TopStart` parity; SwiftUI
   `ZStack` defaults to `.center`). A **stack** (`VStack`/`HStack`) reads a
   **single axis** of the same code — the `VStack` cross-axis is horizontal
   (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), the `HStack` cross-axis vertical
   (`0/1/2` = top/center/bottom).
 - **Overflow**: a Fixed box constrains layout but does not clip — content that
   exceeds it is drawn outside the box unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it
   (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity).
 - **Edge cases**: the first child is **not** a special "background" — it follows
   the same size model (a Fixed first child keeps its exact box; a `Fill` one
   stretches); draw order is child index, with an explicit `Z_INDEX` overriding it
   (higher = on top, equal → child index); a `Fill` child in a Hug ZStack
   propagates (fills the parent's proposal).
 
 ### Grid — `GRID` 0x13
 
 Static 2D matrix grid, eagerly rendered with aligned rows & columns. Children
 are cells, **row-major in insertion order** — child *i* occupies the cell at
 `(row = i / columns, column = i % columns)`. **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (a 2D
 position code applied per-cell, like `ZStack` — the [ZStack alignment
 table](#zstack--zstack-0x12)), `SPACING`
 (uniform row + column gap), `GRID_COLUMNS` (column count), `GRID_ROWS` (row
 count), plus layout modifiers (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frames — the grid's box, never a
 count — `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset).
 
 #### The grid layout model
 
 `GRID` (and the lazy grids) follow the **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose grid model**:
 a grid *proposes* a size to each cell, the cell reports its own size, and the
 grid *places* it at its track intersection. Unlike a stack, a grid has no main
 axis — its two track axes (columns × rows) follow the size model
 [above](#the-stack-layout-model) independently, with two differences:
 
 **Cell counts.** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) is the **column count** and
 `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`) the **row count**. A **Fixed** value pins that count;
 **`FILL` or absent means auto-fit** — the grid derives the count from the number
 of cells and the available space (Compose `GridCells.Fixed(N)` vs `Adaptive`;
 SwiftUI `LazyVGrid(columns:)` / `LazyHGrid(rows:)`). They are **constructor
 properties** (never chainable modifiers) and are **never pixel sizes**.
 
 **Tracks.** On a **fixed-count** axis the tracks are **equal `1fr` fractions**
 of the grid's size on that axis (`repeat(N, 1fr)` in CSS, Compose
 `GridCells.Fixed`, SwiftUI `.flexible()` columns): every track gets the same
 share. A Hug grid on that axis sizes the tracks to the content instead (each
 track as large as its widest/tallest cell) and hugs to the content + `SPACING`.
 The **auto** axis always sizes tracks to the content — each row/column is
 exactly as large as its cells need.
 
 **Per-track sizes (`GRID_TRACKS`).** For per-track control a grid may carry a
 **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) constructor property — a comma-separated
 track list, one entry per track on the fixed-count axis, **taking precedence**
 over `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` (a bare count is the `N`×`flexible` sugar). Each
 entry is:
 
 | Token | Meaning | CSS | Compose | SwiftUI |
 |-------|---------|-----|---------|---------|
 | `flex` | equal `1fr` share (the count's track) | `1fr` | `GridCells.Fixed` column | `.flexible()` |
 | `fixed:<points>` | exactly `<points>` wide | `<points>px` | fixed dp column | `.fixed(_:)` |
 | `adaptive:<points>` | auto-fit, at least `<points>` (fit as many as fit) | `minmax(<points>px,1fr)` | `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize)` | `.adaptive(minimum:)` |
 
 The track list is **CSS-grid-native** — renderers whose native grid has no
 per-track sizing equivalent (GTK `GtkGrid`) size tracks naturally instead
 (renderer status, not a protocol contract).
 
 **Spacing.** `SPACING` is a **uniform gap between tracks on both axes** — the
 row gap and the column gap are the same value (Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy`,
 CSS `gap`), clamped to ≥ 0, never before the first or after the last track.
 
 **Per-cell allocation.** Each cell keeps its own size on both axes (a Fixed box,
 or Hug content) and is **positioned** within its track by the grid's `ALIGNMENT`
 (a **2D position code**, like `ZStack` — the [table
 above](#zstack--zstack-0x12)) — e.g. `0`/absent = top-leading, `3` = top-center.
 Position-only: it never resizes a cell. Only a **`Fill`-sized cell** (or a
 greedy filler like `COLOR`) stretches to fill its track.
 
 **Own size & edge cases.** A grid follows the universal size model: **Hug**
 (content tracks + `SPACING`), a Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` **box**, or **`Fill`**
 (expands to the parent's proposal). `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` never size the
 grid — they only set the track counts. A grid **never propagates** a `Fill` cell
 up to a Hug parent — a `Fill` cell fills its own track, and the grid's own size
 comes from its own frame. Negative `SPACING` → 0; a Fixed box constrains layout
 but does not clip (`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips).
 
 ### GridRow — `GRID_ROW` 0x1D
 
 An **explicit row grouping** for a `GRID` (the SwiftUI `GridRow` authoring
 surface): a grid's children are **cells or `GRID_ROW`s**, and a `GRID_ROW`'s
 children are the cells of **one row**. It lets the author control row layout
 directly instead of relying on row-major index flow.
 
 - **Row placement.** A `GRID_ROW` always starts a new row: its children are
   placed left-to-right in that row starting at column 0, then the row advances.
   **Bare cells** (direct `GRID` children) auto-flow row-major, advancing to the
   next row after `GRID_COLUMNS` cells (or auto, below).
 - **Column count.** The equal-`1fr` track count is `GRID_COLUMNS` when set;
   otherwise the **widest row** (a `GRID_ROW` or a bare-cell run) defines it. A
   short row leaves its trailing columns **empty** — a cell never pulls the next
   row's cells forward.
 - **Structure.** A `GRID_ROW` is structural only: it renders nothing outside a
   `GRID` (like `COMMENT`), and renderers flatten its cells into the grid's rows.
   Its own `ALIGNMENT`/`SPACING`/size properties are ignored.
 - **Example.** `Grid { GridRow { A; B }; GridRow { C; D }; E }` lays out row 0 =
   `A B`, row 1 = `C D`, row 2 = `E` (auto-flowing to the next row after the two
   columns defined by the widest row).
 
 ### ScrollView — `SCROLLVIEW` 0x14
 
 A scrollable content container. **Layout-greedy on its scroll axis** — it fills
 the available space on that axis so the content can scroll; on the **cross axis**
 it **hugs its content** by default (it shrinks to fit the content, SwiftUI
 `ScrollView` semantics). An explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides either behavior
 (LAYOUT.md §layout-greedy primitives). A finite `MAX_WIDTH`/`MAX_HEIGHT` caps
 the greedy scroll-axis size and any cross-axis fill propagation
 (LAYOUT.md §frame bounds); the capped viewport is positioned by the parent's
 `ALIGNMENT`.
 
 **Properties**: `SCROLL_AXIS` (0x0021, F32 enum: `Vertical`=0 — the default when
 absent, `Horizontal`=1) selects the scroll axis; plus layout modifiers
 (Fixed/Fill frames, `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset).
 
 **Content.** The **first child** is the content; a scroll view carries a single
 content subtree (typically a stack), matching SwiftUI/Compose's single-content
 contract. The content is measured with an **unbounded proposal on the scroll
 axis** — it may grow beyond the viewport (that is what scrolls) — and a
 **bounded proposal on the cross axis** (the viewport's cross size). **Fill
 propagation applies on the cross axis**: a `Fill`-width child of the content
 stack (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` in SwiftUI) is itself `Fill`-sized and
 fills the viewport on that axis — so a full-width scroll row is authored as a
 `Fill`-width child, never by stretching the content or the viewport. Content
 with no `Fill` child keeps its natural cross size, and the viewport hugs/shrinks
 to fit it. The **viewport** is the scroll view's allocated box; a Hug
 `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` — or a Hug parent proposal on an axis — sizes the viewport to
 the content's natural size on that axis (the viewport fits the content, so that
 axis does not scroll).
 
 **Overflow.** A scroll view scrolls its content rather than clipping it — the
 viewport clips by virtue of scrolling; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` on the scroll view has
 no further effect on the content.
 
 **Events.** With the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8) the renderer reports the
 content offset in logical points via `EVENT::SCROLL`; with `WHEEL` (bit 9) it
 reports wheel/trackpad deltas via `EVENT::WHEEL` (both draft — see
 [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)).
 
 ### LazyVGrid — `LAZY_VGRID` 0x15
 
 Virtualized vertical grid. **Allocation is identical to `GRID`** — row-major
 cells, `GRID_COLUMNS` = column count (Fixed pins it, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit),
 equal `1fr` columns, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment, hug-to-content
-own size. The only difference is **realization**: a renderer MAY defer realizing
-off-screen cells until scrolled into view and MAY discard realized cells that
-leave the viewport. Realization never changes layout — a cell's position is
-always its row-major index in the full cell list. Typically nested inside a
-`SCROLLVIEW`.
+own size. Typically nested inside a `SCROLLVIEW`. This version defines no grid
+window; a `LAZY_VGRID` without one allocates and realizes like `GRID`.
 
 ### LazyHGrid — `LAZY_HGRID` 0x16
 
 Virtualized horizontal grid; the flipped-axis form of `LAZY_VGRID`. **Allocation
 is identical to `GRID` mirrored**: cells are **column-major** in insertion
 order, `GRID_ROWS` = row count (Fixed pins it, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit), equal
-`1fr` rows, columns auto-flow, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment,
-windowed realization.
+`1fr` rows, columns auto-flow, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment. Like
+`LAZY_VGRID`, this version has no grid window contract and realizes like
+`GRID`.
 
 ### LazyVStack — `LAZY_VSTACK` 0x1B
 
-Virtualized vertical stack. **Allocation is identical to `VStack`** (the stack
-layout model above — same properties, sizing, spacing, alignment, and fill
-propagation); only **realization** differs: a renderer MAY defer realizing
-children outside the visible region.
+A **virtualized vertical stack**. With no window properties it allocates and
+realizes exactly like `VStack` (same sizing, spacing, alignment, and fill
+propagation). With a data-source window it carries:
 
+| Property | Value | Type | Meaning |
+|----------|-------|------|---------|
+| `ITEM_COUNT` | `0x0022` | U32 | Total items in the virtual list |
+| `ITEM_EXTENT` | `0x0023` | F32 | Uniform main-axis size of one item (logical points) |
+| `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` | `0x0024` | U32 | Absolute index of the first emitted child (default 0) |
+
+The data source is **app-owned**: the application emits only the visible items
+and declares the total count. The renderer reports the visible index range with
+`EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` (listener bit 10), and the application re-emits the
+window. `ITEM_COUNT` and a positive `ITEM_EXTENT` together enable windowing; if
+either is absent (or `ITEM_EXTENT` is not positive), the node is an eager
+`VStack`.
+
+**Layout.** The container occupies the full virtual main-axis extent
+`ITEM_COUNT*ITEM_EXTENT + max(0, ITEM_COUNT-1)*SPACING`. Emitted child `j` is
+absolute item `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j` and is placed at
+`(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(ITEM_EXTENT+SPACING)`; the child is constrained to
+`ITEM_EXTENT` on the main axis. Cross-axis behavior, alignment, fill
+propagation, and clipping are the `VStack` contract. The full contract is in
+[LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](./LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-stacks).
+
+**Events.** A node with listener bit 10 (`VISIBLE_RANGE`) receives
+`EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` with the first visible absolute index and the visible
+count. See [EVENTS.md §Visible range](./EVENTS.md#visible-range).
+
 ### LazyHStack — `LAZY_HSTACK` 0x1C
 
-Virtualized horizontal stack. **Allocation is identical to `HStack`**; only
-realization is windowed.
+The horizontal form of `LAZY_VSTACK`: same window properties, virtual extent,
+and `VISIBLE_RANGE` reporting with the main axis horizontal (`ITEM_EXTENT` is a
+width). Without window properties it is an eager `HStack`.
 
 ### SizeThatFits — `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17
 
 A **fit slot**: it shows **one child at a time — the currently selected
 candidate**. In the **live (delta) form** only that child is ever transmitted:
 the app owns the candidates (their views never ride the wire) and transmits the
 **fit query** (`FIT_QUERY`, LIST — the candidates' `minWidth` thresholds,
 ascending) plus the selected child. In a **full-snapshot emission** (the web SSR
 first document), every candidate is transmitted as a child — the renderer renders
 all branches and the browser selects the matching one (see the visibility
 contract below) so the first paint is already correct. The renderer measures its
 **own allocated width** (the slot is size-taking — it stretches to its parent's
 proposal, never hugs, so it always has a well-defined width) and selects the fit
 **locally**:
 
 > **Fit rule** — the selected index is `max{ i : thresholds[i] ≤ measured
 > width }` (threshold 0 candidate always qualifies — the fallback); equal
 > thresholds pick the **lower index**; before the first measure the app renders
 > the threshold-0 candidate (index 0). The measurement is in **logical points**,
 > so the pick is identical on every renderer given the same slot width.
 
 The renderer reports its selection back with **`FIT_CHANGED`** ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md))
 — emitted **once after the first measure, and then only when the derived fit
 index changes** (a band crossing). It never streams the raw size. The app reacts
 by swapping the slot's child (a `TREE` delta pair); a selection that maps to the
 already-shown view re-emits **zero** opcodes. After a **full-snapshot**
 presentation (all candidates laid out), the first `FIT_CHANGED` is the signal
 that collapses the slot back to the live single-selected-child form.
 
 **Candidate identity (MUST).** The candidate **index `i`** is the candidate's
 position in the **ascending `FIT_QUERY` table** (equal thresholds keep the app's
 surface order). In a **full-snapshot emission** the slot's **child order MUST
 equal `FIT_QUERY` order** — the child at position `i` is candidate `i`. The fit
 rule, the `FIT_CHANGED` payload, and the CSS gate all use this one mapping. A
 candidate declared first in the DSL but carrying a **higher** `minWidth` is
 therefore **not** index 0.
 
 **Full-snapshot visibility (MUST).** In a full-snapshot emission the renderer
 MUST show **exactly one** candidate — the one at `index(w)` for the slot's own
 allocated width `w` — with no JS:
 
 - the slot's own width is the query context (each slot is measured
   independently);
 - each candidate is gated behind a marker carrying its `FIT_QUERY` index;
 - for every threshold `T_i` with `i ≥ 1` there is a **band** that, at
   `w ≥ T_i`, makes candidate `i` visible and **hides every candidate `j ≠ i`**;
   bands are emitted **ascending** so the highest matching band wins; no band
   exists for `T_0`;
 - the per-candidate **default** (below the first band / no match) is candidate
   `0` visible, every other candidate hidden;
 - **invariant**: exactly one candidate is visible at every width.
 
 **Hydration collapse (MUST).** After the first `FIT_CHANGED` the app swaps the
 slot to the live single-selected-child form (the unselected candidates leave as
 `TREE` deltas) and the renderer removes the full-snapshot gating — the gate
 markers, the query context, and the band rules — so no CSS gate remains; a
 `FIT_CHANGED` that maps to the already-shown candidate re-emits **zero** opcodes.
 
 The collapse is signalled by the **removal of a candidate** (a `TREE` `REMOVE_CHILD`
 /`DELETE_NODE` on the slot), not by an arbitrary structural op. A **full-snapshot
 emission replayed as opcodes** (e.g. `META::RESYNC`) therefore does **not** collapse
 the slot: the renderer reuses its existing gate (the SSR gate markers + band rules)
 and keeps showing the width-correct candidate. The app's retained tree stays in the
 snapshot form until the first `FIT_CHANGED` downgrade actually removes a candidate.
 
 The concrete web realization (CSS container + per-candidate gate wrappers +
 `@container` band rules) is **renderer-owned** and described in
 `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`.
 
 **Shared subtrees in a full snapshot (MUST).** When the same subtree is authored
 inside more than one candidate, a full-snapshot emission materializes that subtree
 **once per candidate** (each candidate renders its own retained nodes). Every copy
 MUST receive a **distinct node id** — no id is reused between candidates, including
 nodes with identity-stable semantics such as a media controller
 ([MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)). The frame's unique-node-id invariant
 ([OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#frame-lifecycle)) therefore holds across the whole slot.
 
 Semantics:
 - **Properties**: `FIT_QUERY` (`0x1039`, LIST).
 - **Events**: `FIT_CHANGED` (`0x13`, host → guest) — reported fit index.
 - **Children**: at most one in the live form; all candidates in a
   full-snapshot emission (the web SSR's first document), in `FIT_QUERY` order.
 - **Renderer statelessness**: the measured width and derived index are layout
   output, not retained application state.
 
 ### ProxyView — `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E
 
 A **proxy view**: a transparent container whose child subtree is served by a
 **different Pathland server**. It lets one app compose views from several
 servers into a single unified document. The proxying server (the app that owns
 the proxy node) connects to the origin server as a Pathland **host** (client),
 receives the origin's subtree, and splices it into its own stream.
 
 - **Protocol**: a container node with **exactly one** child in the live form —
   the origin subtree's root. The origin subtree's nodes are ordinary nodes of
   the same protocol; the proxying server has **remapped their node ids** into a
   disjoint high range so they never collide with the proxying app's own ids.
 - **Layout**: a **transparent passthrough** container. It imposes no spacing or
   alignment of its own; it proposes its own allocated size to its single child
   and, unless the app constrains it (`frame`/size modifiers), sizes to that
   child. Renderers render it as a plain container (a box/`div`) — there is no
   proxy-specific native element.
 - **Events**: raw events whose target id falls in a proxy's remapped range are
   the origin server's; the proxying server forwards them (id remapped back) to
   the origin over the origin connection rather than dispatching them locally.
 - **Ownership**: the proxy node belongs to the proxying app's retained tree; the
   child subtree belongs to the origin server's retained tree. The proxying app
   never diffs the origin subtree — it forwards the origin's deltas verbatim
   (id-remapped). A **full-snapshot** (`META::RESYNC`) of the proxying app embeds
   the origin's current snapshot; the origin snapshot is requested with a
   `META::RESYNC` sent to the origin server (there is no proxy-specific opcode).
 - **Renderer statelessness**: a renderer applies the remapped origin opcodes
   like any other opcodes; it holds no notion of "remote".
 
 The full contract — id namespacing, the snapshot/`RESYNC` handshake, event
 routing, SSR embedding, and the backpressure policy — is specified in
 [PROXY.md](./PROXY.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## C. Semantic Control Nodes
 
 Semantic controls encapsulate intent, two-way bindings, accessibility traits,
 and local interaction physics. Rendering follows the [Dual-Mode Rendering
 Pipeline](#2-dual-mode-rendering-pipeline--platform-delegation): **Native Token
 Mode** when the node has no children; **Composite Override Mode** when it does.
 
 ### Button — `BUTTON` 0x20
 
 An action trigger control.
 
 | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
 |----------|----|------|---------|
 | label text | `SET_TEXT` / `TEXT` | STRING | The button's text label (leaf mode fallback) |
 | `ACTION_ID` | 0x2016 | U32 | Callback id that gates event delivery (Event Guards) |
 | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (bound to the action's value, if any) |
 | `ENABLED` | 0x2003 | U8 | 1 = interactive, 0 = disabled |
 | `STATE` | 0x2002 | F32 (enum) | Accessibility state (see OPCODE.md) |
 | `EVENT_LISTENERS` | 0x2005 | U32 | Raw pointer listeners (down/move/up) for app-side tap composition |
 | `COLOR`/`FONT_*`/`PADDING`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/… | — | — | Text & appearance modifiers (MODIFIERS.md) |
 
 - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** no children → native button; the label is the
   node's text (`SET_TEXT`). If the text is also absent, render an empty
   platform button shell (leaf fallback). Button styles are renderer/token-owned.
 - **Composite Override Mode (container):** children present → suppress default
   button chrome, render the custom label tree, wrap it with a native
   click/press gesture that reports `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` for the button's
   `ACTION_ID` callback.
 - **Events:** the tap is the app-side composition of the raw pointer events
   (`POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same target). Without `ACTION_ID` /
   `BINDING_ID` / `EVENT_LISTENERS`, a renderer MUST drop the interaction (Event
   Guards).
 - **Note (SwiftUI `Link`)**: SwiftUI's `Link` is `BUTTON` with an associated
   URL; the app handles the tap and opens the URL. No separate primitive.
 
 ### TextField / SecureField — `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21
 
 Single-line text input; `SecureField` is the same component with `IS_SECURE`.
 
 | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
 |----------|----|------|---------|
 | `LABEL` | 0x200A | STRING | Caption label |
 | `PROMPT` | 0x200B | STRING | Placeholder text |
 | `IS_SECURE` | 0x200D | U8 | 1 = masked input (`SecureField`) |
 | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (text value) |
 | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
 
 - **Events** (see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)): `TEXT_CHANGED` (0x07) on every
   edit; `FOCUS_CHANGED` (0x08), `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09), `SUBMIT` (0x0A) —
   draft. All gated by `BINDING_ID` or the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits.
 - **Security**: a secure field MUST mask characters and MUST NOT echo the value.
 
 ### TextEditor — `TEXT_EDITOR` 0x22
 
 Multi-line text editing area.
 
 - **Protocol**: a leaf node; content via `SET_TEXT`, value binding via
   `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
 - **Properties**: `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
   `IS_SECURE` (unused), text modifiers.
 - **Events**: same as `TextField` — `TEXT_CHANGED` (0x07), `FOCUS_CHANGED`
   (0x08), `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09), `SUBMIT` (0x0A) — gated by `BINDING_ID` /
   `EVENT_LISTENERS`.
 
 ### Toggle — `TOGGLE` 0x24
 
 A boolean switch, checkbox, or button control. The **visual style is a token**,
 not a separate component:
 
 | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
 |----------|----|------|---------|
 | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | 0x2018 | F32 (enum) | `Switch`=0 (default), `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
 | `SELECTED` | 0x2004 | U8 | Checked state (0 off, 1 on) |
 | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (bool value) |
 | `LABEL` | 0x200A | STRING | Optional caption |
 | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
 
 - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** renders the native control for the
   `TOGGLE_STYLE` token — a native switch, checkbox, or toggle button. The style
   token switches native variants **without emitting child nodes**.
 - **Composite Override Mode (container):** a custom body (e.g. label + icon)
   wrapped with a native toggle gesture; `SELECTED` still drives the state.
 - **Events:** a user change emits `VALUE_CHANGED` (0x06) with `B` = 0/1 — gated
   by `BINDING_ID`. The app writes it into `SELECTED`; the engine re-emits the
   `SELECTED` property.
 
 ### Slider — `SLIDER` 0x25
 
 A continuous or stepped numeric range control.
 
 | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
 |----------|----|------|---------|
 | `VALUE` | 0x2006 | F32 | Current value |
 | `MIN_VALUE` | 0x2007 | F32 | Inclusive minimum |
 | `MAX_VALUE` | 0x2008 | F32 | Inclusive maximum |
 | `STEP_VALUE` | 0x2009 | F32 | Stepped mode increment (default 1.0 if absent; absent = continuous) |
 | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (numeric value) |
 | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
 
 - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** native slider; the renderer owns 120 FPS
   client-side thumb dragging and resolves the semantic value from its own track
   geometry.
 - **Composite Override Mode (container):** a custom track/thumb body wrapped
   with a native drag gesture that reports `VALUE_CHANGED`.
 - **Events:** `VALUE_CHANGED` (0x06, `A=targetId, B=value (f32)`) — gated by
   `BINDING_ID`.
 
 ### Stepper — `STEPPER` 0x26
 
 A discrete increment/decrement control. `VALUE` (0x2006), `STEP_VALUE`
 (0x2009), `MIN_VALUE` (0x2007), `MAX_VALUE` (0x2008), `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
 Events: `VALUE_CHANGED` after each press.
 
 ### DatePicker — `DATE_PICKER` 0x27
 
 A date & time selection modal/popover control.
 
 - **Protocol**: a leaf node whose value is set with the **`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`**
   command (draft 0x04, see OPCODE.md): `A=nodeId, B=days since epoch (I32,
   pre-1970 negative), C=millis of day (U32, 0..86,400,000)`.
 - **Properties**: `DATE_PICKER_MODE` (0x2013, enum: `Date`=0, `Time`=1,
   `DateAndTime`=2), `BINDING_ID` (0x2017), size modifiers.
 - **Events**: `DATE_CHANGED` (draft 0x0D, `A=targetId, B=days (I32),
   C=millis of day (U32)`) — inline, gated by `BINDING_ID`.
 
 ### Picker — `PICKER` 0x28
 
 A selection control rendered as a segment, dropdown menu, or wheel.
 
 - **Protocol**: a container node whose **children are the options**, in display
   order (each a leaf whose text is the option label) — the same "options are
   children" rule as `Menu` action items.
 - **Properties**: `SELECTION` (0x2010, U32 child index), `PICKER_STYLE`
   (0x2014, enum: `Menu`=0, `Segmented`=1, `Wheel`=2, `RadioGroup`=3),
   `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
 - **Events**: `VALUE_CHANGED` with `B` = the new selected child index — gated
   by `BINDING_ID`.
 
 ### Menu — `MENU` 0x29
 
 A **semantic control**: contextual action trigger and popover container. The
 client platform owns dynamic popover presentation, overlay placement, tap/focus
 management, and accessibility focus trapping.
 
 #### Dual-Mode Rendering Rules
 
 - **Native Token Mode (Leaf Trigger):** with no custom trigger child node, the
   client MUST render its native system drop-down button shell using the
   designated trigger label property (the node's text via `SET_TEXT`, or
   `LABEL` 0x200A).
 - **Composite Override Mode (Custom Trigger Container):** when a custom view
   tree (e.g. an `HStack` with an avatar image and text label) is designated as
   the menu trigger, the client MUST:
   1. suppress default OS drop-down button styling,
   2. render the custom trigger layout tree sent by the server,
   3. wrap that custom layout tree with native menu tap/click handlers, hover
      states, and popover anchor bindings.
 
 #### Child Composition Rules
 
 A `Menu` manages **two types of child view trees**:
 
 1. **Trigger View** — the custom layout tree representing the clickable visual
    trigger element.
 2. **Action Items** — child semantic nodes representing menu options (`Button`,
    `Toggle`, or nested sub-`Menu` nodes).
 
 Renderers **MUST** map child `Button` and `Toggle` nodes inside a `Menu` directly
 to **native OS menu item slots** rather than standard canvas/layout nodes.
 
 - **Events**: `VALUE_CHANGED` with `B` = the chosen action item index — gated
   by `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
 
 ### ColorPicker — `COLOR_PICKER` 0x2A
 
 A native system color picker control.
 
 - **Protocol**: a leaf node with `COLOR_VALUE` (0x2012, COLOR — packed
   `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB) and `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
 - **Events**: `VALUE_CHANGED` — the value field carries the packed color **as an
   f32 bit pattern** of `0xAARRGGBB` (the app reinterprets it) — gated by
   `BINDING_ID`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Reserved component type IDs
 
 | Range | Use |
 |-------|-----|
 | `0x01`–`0x08`, `0x0A`–`0x0B` | Primitive drawing & visual nodes (allocated, this file) |
 | `0x09`, `0x0C`–`0x0F` | Future drawing nodes (unallocated; `0x09` formerly `AUDIO`) |
 | `0x10`–`0x16`, `0x1B`–`0x1E` | Layout & container primitives (this file) |
 | `0x17`–`0x1A` | Reserved (formerly composites) — never reused |
 | `0x1F` | Future layout nodes (unallocated) |
 | `0x20`–`0x22`, `0x24`–`0x2A` | Semantic control nodes (this file) |
 | `0x23`, `0x2B`–`0x2F` | Future semantic controls (unallocated) |
 | `0x30` | `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (non-visual/resource, this file) |
 | `0x31`–`0x7E` | Future categories (unallocated) |
 | `0x7F` | `COMMENT` (utility) |
 | `0x80`–`0xFF` | Reserved |
 | `0x0100`–`0xFFFF` | Application/custom component types |
 
 A renderer MUST handle an unknown component type by rendering a blank node and
 continuing — it must not crash or stop decoding.
 
 ---
 
 ## Conformance
 
 Each primitive's opcode footprint is covered by the golden vectors in
 [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md). New primitives added here MUST add vectors
 before implementation lands in any renderer.

# ADR-0013: SwiftUI-shaped authoring with signal-based reactivity

**Status:** Accepted
**Recorded:** 2026-11-12 (extracted existing decision; original date not established)
**Scope:** Authoring DSLs, signals, component reconciliation

## Context

Different languages need idiomatic authoring surfaces that map to the same
protocol. Reactive structural composition and fine-grained property updates
must coexist without changing the wire model.

## Decision

Use SwiftUI-shaped view/modifier vocabulary with Angular-style writable signals,
computeds, effects, and bindings rather than SwiftUI property wrappers. Reads in
a component's tracked `body()` subscribe that component; direct node bindings
retain fine-grained updates. Keep modifiers decoupled from view types.

## Rationale

The DSL contract explicitly separates familiar view syntax from the reactivity
model. It allows plain host-language control flow in tracked bodies and direct
signal binding without rerunning the body. Both paths still emit only actual
changes through the same engine contract.

## Alternatives

SwiftUI `@State`/`@Binding` wrappers are explicitly distinguished from the chosen
signal model. View-type-specific modifier mechanisms are excluded by the DSL
contract. The sources do not establish a historical comparison with other
reactivity libraries.

## Consequences

Conformant language DSLs must agree on semantics and opcode output, not merely
similar names. Component bodies must respect the contract's purity rules.
Authoring syntax can adapt to language constraints without reallocating wire
IDs or changing protocol meanings.

## Sources and current contract

- [DSL guiding rules](../../spec/DSL.md#two-guiding-rules).
- [Authoring principles](../../spec/DSL.md#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored).
- [Engine emission contract](../../spec/ENGINE.md#5-reactive-emission).

### ADR-0014

Title: Virtualized lazy stacks through app-owned data sources

Status: Accepted
Recorded: 2026-11-12
Scope: Authoring DSL, engine emission, lazy container layout, renderer realization, SSR first paint
Supersedes: None (clarifies the realization wording in spec/PRIMITIVES.md)

Context:
- Lazy containers exist by ID but are aliases of eager containers.
- Goal: thousands of rows, only visible rendered.
- Constraints: 4096-slot ring, 1 MiB arena, renderer statelessness, renderer cannot size unrealized rows, SSR has no viewport at first paint.
- SwiftUI-shaped authoring is required (ADR-0013); no parallel `VirtualVStack`.

Decision:
- `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` + `ForEach` data source.
- App owns data + row builder; engine owns window.
- Fixed uniform extent inferred from row's fixed main-axis frame or explicit `itemExtent`.
- Protocol: ITEM_COUNT, ITEM_EXTENT, FIRST_ITEM_INDEX; VISIBLE_RANGE event; listener bit 10.
- Virtual extent formula; window placement.
- Window reconcile by absolute index/key.
- SSR first window + full virtual extent.
- v1 stacks only; grids follow.

Rationale:
- O(window) app/wire/memory; renderer only realizes visible; fits stateless renderer; matches FIT_CHANGED precedent; maintains SwiftUI shape.

Alternatives:
- Renderer-owned windowing (all children sent): O(N), ring overflow, can't size unrealized.
- Renderer pull: more protocol/async surface.
- Variable height first: complexity; deferred.
- Parallel VirtualVStack: rejected for authoring confusion.
- Full SSR: O(N) HTML.

Consequences:
- New properties/event/listener bit; engine window state; keyed reconcile; renderer work; SSR first window; row state limitation; a11y; grids deferred; variable height deferred.

Sources:
- spec/PRIMITIVES.md lazy sections, LAYOUT.md, EVENTS.md, OPCODE.md, DSL.md; ADR-0002, 0003, 0011, 0013.

# Pathland Core Modifiers

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 1, 2026

---

## Purpose

This document is the **catalog of core modifiers** the Pathland protocol must
support. In the protocol these are the **`PARAMETER` properties**: the constraint
properties and visual decorations carried by `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`. The set
mirrors SwiftUI's core modifiers so that any SwiftUI-shaped UI can be expressed.

Like SwiftUI, modifiers in Pathland are **decoupled from views**: any modifier
applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A
modifier that a particular renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** —
the property is still emitted; the renderer skips it. Application code composes
custom modifiers from these core ones.

- View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
- Wire format and value types: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
- Events: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)

> **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
> in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
> defines the protocol contract only.

### Emission rules

Each modifier emits **one or more** `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` opcodes — one per
underlying property. There is no compound-modifier opcode. Compound SwiftUI
modifiers (`.frame(width:height:alignment:)`, `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)`,
`.border(_:width:)`) are expanded into several `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes, exactly
as the existing `.frame` modifier already does (`WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` +
`ALIGNMENT`).

`SET_PROPERTY` packing (see OPCODE.md):

```
A = nodeId
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
C = value (f32 bit pattern / u32 / u8 / color / arenaRef)
```

Only **changed** properties emit: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes
(diff-based reactive emission). `STRING`-valued properties carry their text in
the frame's string section; `C` holds the arena offset.

### Value types (from `value_type`, u8)

| Value Type | Value | `C` encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------|
| `U8` | 0x01 | low byte of C |
| `U32` | 0x02 | u32 |
| `I32` | 0x03 | i32 |
| `F32` | 0x04 | f32 bit pattern |
| `STRING` | 0x05 | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | 0x06 | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | 0x07 | packed `0xAARRGGBB` (sRGB) |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x08 | arenaRef (token path) |

Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1.0` = `FILL` (expand to available), `-2.0` =
`HUG_CONTENT` (native intrinsic size).

> **`maxWidth`/`maxHeight: .infinity`**: SwiftUI's flexible frame is expressed as
> the `FILL` sentinel on `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`. DSLs accept `∞` (e.g. Rust
> `f32::INFINITY`, Java `Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY`) and normalize it to `FILL`
> before emission, so `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` ⇔ `WIDTH = FILL`. The
> renderer then expands the element to the available space.

> **Token references**: every property typed `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM`
> in the tables below MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`),
> with `C` = arenaRef to a token path — so modifiers like `.foregroundStyle`,
> `.tint`, `.background`, `.border(color:)`, `.shadow(color:)`, `.font(size:)`,
> `.padding(_:)`, `.cornerRadius(_:)`, `.frame(width:height:)`, and `.spacing(_:)`
> accept either a literal or a token reference. The renderer resolves the
> reference against the [token catalog and color schemes](./TOKENS.md).

## 1. Layout

Arrangement and sizing. These map to the native renderer's layout knobs.

| SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
| `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 | F32, F32, ENUM | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided axis/alignment; `ALIGNMENT` is optional — when omitted (width-only / width+height frames), a stack's own cross-axis alignment is preserved |
| `.frame(minWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:maxHeight:)` | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012, `MAX_WIDTH` 0x0014, `MIN_HEIGHT` 0x0015, `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 | F32 | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided bound; `0x0013`/`0x0016` are retired |
| `.padding(_:)`, `.padding(edges:)`, `.padding(_:edges:)` | `PADDING` 0x1011, `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012, `PADDING_RIGHT` 0x1013, `PADDING_BOTTOM` 0x1014, `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 | F32 | uniform → one; per-edge → per-edge |
| `.offset(x:y:)` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F | F32 | two |
| `.position(x:y:)` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 | F32 | two |
| `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 | U8 (0/1) | two (or one when axis-limited) |
| `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A | F32 | one |
| `.zIndex(_:)` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F | F32 | one | Draw-order override in an overlapping container (`ZStack`/grid): higher = on top, equal → child index (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack) |
| `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | F32, ENUM | two |
| `.scaledToFit()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fit`=0) | one |
| `.scaledToFill()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fill`=1) | one |
| `.imageSource(_:)` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` 0x1002 | STRING (asset reference) | one (arenaRef) |
| `.mediaSource(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_SOURCE` 0x103B | STRING (asset reference) | one (arenaRef) |
| `.mediaController(_:)` (Video) | `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` 0x103A | U32 (the controller node id) | one |
| `.playback(_:)` (MediaController) | `PLAYBACK_STATE` 0x1035 | U32 (0 pause, 1 play) | one |
| `.mediaPosition(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_POSITION` 0x1036 | F32 (seconds; change = seek) | one |
| `.mediaVolume(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_VOLUME` 0x1037 | F32 (0..1) | one |
| `.mediaMuted(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_MUTED` 0x103C | U8 (0/1) | one |
| `.mediaLoop(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_LOOP` 0x103D | U8 (0/1) | one |
| `.mediaRate(_:)` (MediaController) | `MEDIA_RATE` 0x103E | F32 (1.0 = normal) | one |
| `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D | F32 | one |
| `.spacing(_:)` (stacks) | `SPACING` 0x0001 | F32 | one |
| `Spacer` | — (implied by component) | — | none |

### Semantics

- **`WIDTH` / `HEIGHT`**: size hints; the renderer maps them to its size
  request / `width`/`height` style. `FILL` (-1.0) expands to available space;
  `HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sizes to intrinsic content. Absence of a property leaves
  that axis to the native default. The full allocation contract — Fixed = an
  exact points box, container space distribution, cross-axis hug-not-stretch,
  content fitting — is in [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).
- **`frame(min/max)`**: each provided bound emits its own property.
  Renderers map them to the native min/max size. The former `IDEAL_WIDTH`
  (`0x0013`) and `IDEAL_HEIGHT` (`0x0016`) ids are retired; do not reuse them.
- **`GRID_COLUMNS` / `GRID_ROWS`** (`0x001E` / `0x001F`, F32) are **constructor
  properties** on grids (never chainable modifiers): the column/row track
  counts. A positive value pins the count (equal `1fr` tracks); `FILL` or absent
  = auto-fit. They never size the grid — the grid's box comes from `WIDTH`/
  `HEIGHT`. See [PRIMITIVES.md §Grid](./PRIMITIVES.md#grid--grid-0x13).
- **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) is the per-track spec — a comma-separated
  `flex` | `fixed:<points>` | `adaptive:<points>` list that takes precedence
  over the counts (the count is `N`×`flex` sugar). CSS-grid-native: renderers
  without a native equivalent size tracks naturally. See PRIMITIVES.md §grid
  model.
- **`PADDING` vs per-edge**: `PADDING` is uniform and shorthand; a per-edge
  modifier overwrites the edge only. Per-edge wins over uniform when both are
  present.
- **`ALIGNMENT` code** (2D position, `0`–`8`): a stack reads a single axis (a
  `VStack` the horizontal component — `0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing — an
  `HStack` the vertical — `0/1/2` = top/center/bottom), a `ZStack`/grid both
  axes (full table in [PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack](./PRIMITIVES.md#zstack--zstack-0x12)).

  resizes them. The cross-axis default is *hug* (children keep their size;
  only `FILL`-sized children stretch). Full contract: [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).

  `Fill`=1 (aspect-fill, cropped).
- **`OFFSET`** moves the element **after** layout without affecting layout
  (post-layout translation).
- **`POSITION`** is absolute placement within the parent; the renderer resolves
  the anchor.

**Notes**: `visible(boolean)` is a Pathland extra (SwiftUI only has
`.hidden()` — `Visible`/`Hidden`). `accessibilityRole`/`accessibilityState`
take raw `int` codes today rather than a typed enum. Raw input listeners are
exposed through the `PointerEvents` modifier value — there is no per-event sugar
(e.g. a `.focusable` or `.onSubmit` that sets the matching bit). `environment`
is the one inheritance/scoping modifier
([§6 rule 6](#6-authoring-conventions)), alongside the style modifiers.

**Window metadata is root-scoped.** `windowMetadata` applies to the whole
hosting surface, not to the subtree it wraps. Values are signals (a plain value
is wrapped as a constant), so a route's title is a `computed` over the router:
`windowMetadata(w -> w.title(computed(() -> titleFor(router.path()))))`. A
signal change re-emits only that `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` field; the renderer
maps it to the window/tab title and description.

### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)

In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.

Media events report a

playback state back to the app — **`A` = the controller node id**, never a media

target is the controller, reporting does not change when a surface is created,

| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |

| `MEDIA_ENDED` | 0x11 | controllerId | 0 | 0 | — | `AVPlayerItemDidPlayToEndTime` |

  background-tab and occluded-window timers throttle to worse cadences). A seek
  initiated by the app (`MEDIA_POSITION` change) is not echoed back.
- **`MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`**: the resource's duration in seconds. Reported when
  the resource loads (or its duration becomes known), and only when it changes —
  never a stream. Gates the useful range of a seek control.
- **`FIT_CHANGED`**: a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot's **selected candidate index** —

# ADR-0014: Virtualized lazy stacks through app-owned data sources

**Status:** Accepted
**Recorded:** 2026-11-12
**Scope:** Authoring DSL, retained-tree emission, lazy container layout, renderer realization, SSR first paint
**Supersedes:** None (refines the lazy-container realization wording in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`)

## Context

Lazy stack and grid component IDs exist (`LAZY_VSTACK`, `LAZY_HSTACK`, `LAZY_VGRID`, `LAZY_HGRID`), but the protocol only says a renderer MAY defer realizing off-screen children. No item count, extent, visible-range request, or window placement exists, so every implementation treats lazy containers as eager aliases. Two constraints make the current wording insufficient:
- The app emits the full child list, and the desktop ring (4096 slots) and arena (1 MiB) cannot carry thousands of rows.
- A renderer cannot position or size an unrealized row without a size model, so it cannot compute scroll extent or decide what is visible.

The authoring surface must remain SwiftUI-shaped (ADR-0013): `LazyVStack(spacing:) { ForEach(items) { ... } }`, not a parallel `VirtualVStack`.

## Decision

Virtualize lazy stacks through an app-owned data source and a renderer-reported visible range.

- `ForEach` inside a `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` is a data source, not an eager child list. Outside a lazy container it keeps eager behavior.
- The app supplies the item collection and row builder; the engine owns the visible window and materializes only the window's rows.
- Fixed uniform extent: the engine derives `ITEM_EXTENT` from the row's fixed main-axis frame (`.frame(height:)` / `.frame(width:)`), or from an explicit `itemExtent` when no fixed frame exists.
- The wire carries `ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, and `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` on the lazy container; the renderer reports `VISIBLE_RANGE` (first index + count) for nodes that declare listener bit 10.
- The lazy container occupies the full virtual main-axis extent (`N*E + max(0,N-1)*S`); emitted child `j` is placed at `(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(E+S)`.
- Window children are reconciled by absolute index (or an optional item key), so ids stay stable while scrolling.
- SSR renders a conservative first window plus the full virtual extent; the client corrects the window after `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
- v1 covers `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK`; lazy grids follow the same model in a later change.

Exact requirements live in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, and `spec/DSL.md`.

## Rationale

- Only the window costs app nodes, wire bytes, renderer model memory, native elements, and SSR HTML; the full list can be arbitrarily large.
- The renderer stays stateless: it reports a measured/derived range, like `FIT_CHANGED`, and the app decides what to emit.
- The app-owned data source keeps the SwiftUI shape and avoids a second lazy authoring vocabulary.
- Fixed extent gives exact scroll extent and window math without measurement passes, matching the fixed-row-height pattern that avoids layout work.
- Windowed SSR avoids O(N) HTML while the full virtual extent keeps the scrollbar correct before JS.

## Alternatives

- **Renderer-owned windowing with all children transmitted.** Rejected: O(N) app tree, wire, and renderer memory; overflows the desktop ring; cannot size unrealized rows; O(N) SSR.
- **Renderer pull by index.** Rejected for v1: adds a request/response handshake and renderer-owned item identity without removing the app's data-source work.
- **A separate `VirtualVStack`/`VirtualHStack` authoring API.** Rejected: confusing alongside `LazyVStack`, and contrary to the SwiftUI-shaped surface.
- **Variable-height first.** Deferred: needs estimation, measurement caching, and scroll anchoring; fixed extent covers the initial large-list use case.
- **Full SSR for every list.** Rejected as the default: O(N) HTML; remains available as an explicit host option for SEO-critical lists.

## Consequences

- New protocol properties (`ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`), event (`VISIBLE_RANGE`), and listener bit (10) require Rust/Java/TS constants, manifest, codec, and conformance updates.
- The engine gains lazy-node window state and a keyed window reconcile; renderers gain virtual-extent placement and range reporting.
- Row-local component state is not preserved when a row leaves the window; apps should keep row state in the data model (keyed state is a follow-up).
- Lazy grids, variable-height rows, native recycling, scroll anchoring, and focused-row pinning remain follow-ups.
- The app must keep a focused row inside its window; the renderer does not auto-pin it.

## Sources and current contract

- Lazy container allocation: `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §LazyVStack/§LazyHStack.
- Virtual extent and placement: `spec/LAYOUT.md` §Virtual extent.
- Event and listener: `spec/EVENTS.md` §Visible range, §Event listeners.
- Properties: `spec/MODIFIERS.md` §Layout.
- Authoring surface: `spec/DSL.md` §4.2.
- Decisions: ADR-0002 (native declarative layout), ADR-0003 (app-owned state and delta emission), ADR-0011 (explicit allocation), ADR-0013 (SwiftUI-shaped DSL).

### EVENT (0x03) — host → guest

The event commands and their `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits are catalogued in
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) (core events, SwiftUI-style); this file defines the
wire encoding.

Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
protocol.

#### Event listeners (which nodes emit events)

A renderer reports raw events only for nodes that declared they want them. The
application declares this intent through the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic
property (`0x2005`, a u32 bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type).
Each bit requests a raw-input event kind (see [`listener`] flags):

| Bit | Mask | Event command | Meaning |
|-----|------|---------------|---------|
| 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` | Report pointer-down for this node |
| 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` | Report pointer-move/enter/leave |
| 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` | Report pointer-up for this node |
| 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` | Report key-down |
| 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` | Report key-up |

> Bits 5–9 (draft) are allocated in [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#event-listeners-event_listeners)
> for `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, and `WHEEL`.
> Value-bearing controls (`SLIDER`, `TOGGLE`, `DATE_PICKER`, …) report their
> value changes by component type and do not need a listener bit.

This is what makes **any element** (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit
events — the renderer attaches native input recognition to the matching native
element when the listener bit is set, not only to buttons. A renderer SHOULD
report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` for a node with the `POINTER_DOWN`/
`POINTER_UP` bits set by attaching a native click/press gesture to that
element.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `POINTER_DOWN` | `0x01` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button pressed at viewport-relative point |
| `POINTER_MOVE` | `0x02` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE` | Pointer moved (bit 0 = entered/hovering, bit 1 = leaving) |
| `POINTER_UP` | `0x03` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button released at viewport-relative point |
| `KEY_DOWN` | `0x04` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` | Key pressed (bit 1 = auto-repeat) |
| `KEY_UP` | `0x05` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | Key released |
| `VALUE_CHANGED` | `0x06` | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | A value-bearing control changed (e.g. slider); the renderer resolves the semantic value from its track geometry |
| `TEXT_CHANGED` | `0x07` | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | A text field's value changed; the new text is a length-prefixed entry in the **event arena** (shared memory, absolute `B` offset) or the batch's string section (network, *relative* `B` offset) — the same dual convention as `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT` |
| `NAVIGATE` | `0x0E` | 0 | URL string offset | 0 | `NAVIGATE_URL` | Global navigation request: with the flag, `B` is the destination URL (browser `popstate`/back/forward/deep-link, same dual string convention as `TEXT_CHANGED`); without the flag, "back one step" (native back affordance). Never node-keyed, never `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#navigation) |

### META (0x04)

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------------|

- Add a subsection after the grid/container notes, maybe before "4.3 Semantic controls". Something like:

```
#### Virtualized lists (`LazyVStack` / `LazyHStack`)

A `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing a `ForEach` is a **windowed data
container**. The app supplies the collection and the row builder; the engine
owns the window and evaluates the builder only for visible rows:

```kotlin
LazyVStack(spacing = 0) {
    ForEach(items) { item, _ ->
        RowView(item)
            .frame(height = 44f)   // fixed main-axis extent
    }
}
```

Rules:

- `ForEach` inside a lazy stack is a **data source**, not an eager child list.
  Outside a lazy stack it keeps eager behavior.
- The lazy stack's content MUST be exactly one `ForEach` for virtualization;
  other children keep the eager stack behavior.
- `ITEM_COUNT` = the collection size. `ITEM_EXTENT` = the row's fixed main-axis

# ADR-0014: Virtualized lazy stacks through app-owned data sources

**Status:** Accepted
**Recorded:** 2026-11-12
**Scope:** Authoring DSL, retained-tree emission, lazy-container layout, renderer realization, SSR first paint
**Supersedes:** None (refines the lazy-container realization wording in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`)

## Context

Lazy stack and grid component IDs exist (`LAZY_VSTACK`, `LAZY_HSTACK`,
`LAZY_VGRID`, `LAZY_HGRID`), but the protocol only says a renderer MAY defer
realizing off-screen children. No item count, extent, visible-range request, or
window placement exists, so every implementation treats lazy containers as eager
aliases. Two constraints make the current wording insufficient:

- The app emits the full child list, and the desktop ring (4096 slots) and arena
  (1 MiB) cannot carry thousands of rows.
- A renderer cannot position or size an unrealized row without a size model, so
  it cannot compute scroll extent or decide what is visible.

The authoring surface must remain SwiftUI-shaped (ADR-0013):
`LazyVStack(spacing:) { ForEach(items) { … } }`, not a parallel
`VirtualVStack`.

## Decision

Virtualize lazy stacks through an app-owned data source and a renderer-reported
visible range.

- `ForEach` inside a `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` is a data source, not an eager
  child list. Outside a lazy container it keeps eager behavior.
- The app supplies the item collection and row builder; the engine owns the
  visible window and materializes only the window's rows.
- Fixed uniform extent: the engine derives `ITEM_EXTENT` from the row's fixed
  main-axis frame (`.frame(height:)` / `.frame(width:)`), or from an explicit
  `itemExtent` when no fixed frame exists.
- The wire carries `ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, and `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` on the
  lazy container; the renderer reports `VISIBLE_RANGE` (first index + count) for
  nodes that declare listener bit 10.
- The lazy container occupies the full virtual main-axis extent
  (`N*E + max(0,N-1)*S`); emitted child `j` is placed at
  `(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(E+S)`.
- Window children are reconciled by absolute index (or an optional item key), so
  ids stay stable while scrolling.
- SSR renders a conservative first window plus the full virtual extent; the
  client corrects the window after `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
- v1 covers `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK`; lazy grids follow the same model in a
  later change.

Exact requirements live in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`,
`spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, and `spec/DSL.md`.

## Rationale

- Only the window costs app nodes, wire bytes, renderer model memory, native
  elements, and SSR HTML; the full list can be arbitrarily large.
- The renderer stays stateless: it reports a measured/derived range, like
  `FIT_CHANGED`, and the app decides what to emit.
- The app-owned data source keeps the SwiftUI shape and avoids a second lazy
  authoring vocabulary.
- Fixed extent gives exact scroll extent and window math without measurement
  passes, matching the fixed-row-height pattern that avoids layout work.
- Windowed SSR avoids O(N) HTML while the full virtual extent keeps the
  scrollbar correct before JavaScript runs.

## Alternatives

- **Renderer-owned windowing with all children transmitted.** Rejected: O(N) app
  tree, wire, and renderer memory; overflows the desktop ring; cannot size
  unrealized rows; O(N) SSR.
- **Renderer pull by index.** Rejected for v1: adds a request/response handshake
  and renderer-owned item identity without removing the app's data-source work.
- **A separate `VirtualVStack`/`VirtualHStack` authoring API.** Rejected:
  confusing alongside `LazyVStack`, and contrary to the SwiftUI-shaped surface.
- **Variable-height first.** Deferred: needs estimation, measurement caching,
  and scroll anchoring; fixed extent covers the initial large-list use case.
- **Full SSR for every list.** Rejected as the default: O(N) HTML; remains
  available as an explicit host option for SEO-critical lists.

## Consequences

- New protocol properties (`ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`),
  event (`VISIBLE_RANGE`), and listener bit (10) require Rust/Java/TS constants,
  manifest, codec, and conformance updates.
- The engine gains lazy-node window state and a keyed window reconcile;
  renderers gain virtual-extent placement and range reporting.
- Row-local component state is not preserved when a row leaves the window; apps
  should keep row state in the data model (keyed state is a follow-up).
- Lazy grids, variable-height rows, native recycling, scroll anchoring, and
  focused-row pinning remain follow-ups.
- The app must keep a focused row inside its window; the renderer does not
  auto-pin it.

## Sources and current contract

- Lazy container allocation: [PRIMITIVES.md §LazyVStack](../../spec/PRIMITIVES.md#lazyvstack--lazy_vstack-0x1b).
- Virtual extent and placement: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-stacks).
- Event and listener: [EVENTS.md §Visible range](../../spec/EVENTS.md#visible-range), [§Event listeners](../../spec/EVENTS.md#event-listeners-event_listeners).
- Properties: [MODIFIERS.md §Layout](../../spec/MODIFIERS.md#1-layout).
- Authoring surface: [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).
- Decisions: [ADR-0002](0002-native-declarative-layout.md),
  [ADR-0003](0003-application-state-and-delta-emission.md),
  [ADR-0011](0011-explicit-layout-allocation.md),
  [ADR-0013](0013-swiftui-shaped-signal-dsl.md).

input.newString:
### LazyVStack — `LAZY_VSTACK` 0x1B

A **virtualized vertical stack**. With no window properties it allocates and
realizes exactly like `VStack` (same sizing, spacing, alignment, and fill
propagation). With a data-source window it carries:

| Property | Value | Type | Meaning |
|----------|-------|------|---------|
| `ITEM_COUNT` | `0x0022` | U32 | Total items in the virtual list |
| `ITEM_EXTENT` | `0x0023` | F32 | Uniform main-axis size of one item (logical points) |
| `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` | `0x0024` | U32 | Absolute index of the first emitted child (default 0) |

The window is **app-owned**: the application emits only the visible items and
declares the total count. The renderer reports the visible index range with
`EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` (listener bit 10), and the application re-emits the
window. `ITEM_COUNT` and `ITEM_EXTENT` together enable windowing; if either is
absent, the node is an eager `VStack`.

**Layout.** The container occupies the full virtual main-axis extent
`ITEM_COUNT*ITEM_EXTENT + max(0, ITEM_COUNT-1)*SPACING`. Emitted child `j` is
absolute item `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j` and is placed at
`(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(ITEM_EXTENT+SPACING)`; the child is constrained to
`ITEM_EXTENT` on the main axis. Cross-axis behavior, alignment, fill
propagation, and clipping are the `VStack` contract. The full contract is in
[LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](./LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-stacks).

**Events.** A node with listener bit 10 (`VISIBLE_RANGE`) receives
`EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` with the first visible absolute index and the visible
count. See [EVENTS.md §Visible range](./EVENTS.md#visible-range).

### LazyHStack — `LAZY_HSTACK` 0x1C

The horizontal form of `LAZY_VSTACK`: same window properties, virtual extent,
and `VISIBLE_RANGE` reporting with the main axis horizontal (`ITEM_EXTENT` is a
width). Without window properties it is an eager `HStack`.

`1fr` rows, columns auto-flow, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment. Like
`LAZY_VGRID`, this version has no grid window contract and realizes like
`GRID`.

### A container that is itself Fixed

A container with a **Fixed** `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` is allocated exactly that box and
lays its children out *within* it. A Fixed box **constrains layout but does not
clip**: content that overflows it is drawn outside the box unless
`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity); it scrolls instead
when the container is a `SCROLLVIEW`.

### Rationale

The choice of explicit allocation and the renderer bugs it addresses are
recorded in [ADR-0011](../docs/decisions/0011-explicit-layout-allocation.md).
The complete allocation requirements remain above.

---

## Content fitting, truncation & clipping

Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:

- **Media** (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`): fitted per `CONTENT_MODE` — `Fit` (0) scales to
  contain (letterboxed), `Fill` (1) scales to cover (cropped). The box is the
  allocation, never the content's intrinsic size. A `VIDEO` surface's playback
  lives on a separate `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node; audio has no visual at all (§
  Non-visual nodes) and is controlled by the application's own views.

### Rationale

The choice of explicit allocation and the renderer bugs it addresses are
recorded in [ADR-0011](../docs/decisions/0011-explicit-layout-allocation.md).
The complete allocation requirements remain above.

---

## Virtual extent (lazy stacks)

A `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` that carries `ITEM_COUNT` (`0x0022`) and
`ITEM_EXTENT` (`0x0023`) is a **windowed data container**. It lays out only the
items the application emitted, but occupies the full list extent so a scroll
viewport reports the correct scrollbar and offsets.

Let `N = ITEM_COUNT`, `E = ITEM_EXTENT`, `S = max(0, SPACING)`, and
`F = FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` (default `0`).

- **Virtual extent** — the container's main-axis size is
  `N*E + max(0, N-1)*S`. `N = 0` gives `0`.
- **Item offset** — absolute item `i` starts at `i*(E+S)`.
- **Window placement** — emitted child `j` is absolute item `F+j` and starts at
  `(F+j)*(E+S)`. Children are emitted in ascending absolute-index order.
- **Child size** — the container constrains each child to exactly `E` on the
  main axis (a Fixed box; overflow is visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`). The
  cross axis is the ordinary stack contract: the child keeps its size and is
  positioned by `ALIGNMENT`; a `Fill`-sized child stretches on the cross axis.
- **Missing children** — the window need not cover every item. Items with no
  emitted child are empty virtual space; the renderer never invents rows.
  Emitted children beyond `N` are ignored.
- **Fill propagation** — the virtual extent is the container's main-axis size;
  it does not propagate `Fill` from a window child on the main axis. Cross-axis
  fill propagation is unchanged.
- **Visible range** — the renderer computes which absolute items intersect the
  nearest scrolling ancestor's viewport (or the root surface when there is
  none): `first = clamp(floor(viewportStart/(E+S)), 0, N)` and
  `endExclusive = clamp(ceil(viewportEnd/(E+S)), 0, N)`. The range is
  conservative: it may include a partially scrolled item, but never excludes a
  visible one. The renderer reports `EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` for nodes with
  listener bit 10, at most once per frame and only when `(first, endExclusive)`
  changes. The application owns overscan and may emit a larger window.

Without `ITEM_COUNT` + `ITEM_EXTENT`, a lazy stack is an ordinary eager stack
and this section does not apply.

parts.text: Now add the visible range section after the Scroll section, before Navigation. The scroll section ends with the WHEEL bullet. Insert.

input.newString:
- **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
  that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
  deltas onto x/y deltas.

### Visible range

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `VISIBLE_RANGE` | 0x15 | targetId | firstIndex (u32) | count (u32) | — | a `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` window |

- **`VISIBLE_RANGE`**: the absolute index range of a windowed lazy container's
  items that intersect the nearest scrolling ancestor's viewport (or the root
  surface when there is none). `B` is the first visible absolute index; `C` is
  the number of visible items.
- Reported only for nodes that declared the `VISIBLE_RANGE` listener bit
  (bit 10) and carry `ITEM_COUNT` (`0x0022`) + `ITEM_EXTENT` (`0x0023`).
- The renderer reports the **current** range after layout, scroll, resize, or a
  count change. It coalesces to at most one event per frame and emits only when
  the derived `(firstIndex, count)` changes. It never streams per-item events.
- The application owns overscan: it may emit a larger window than the reported
  range. The renderer reports the visible range, not the app's window.
- `count = 0` is valid (the container is empty or entirely off-screen).
- The range math is specified in
  [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](./LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-stacks).

### Navigation

the counts; a count is the `N`×`flexible` sugar. CSS-grid-native — renderers
without a native per-track equivalent size tracks naturally (renderer status,
spec/PRIMITIVES.md §grid model).

#### Virtualized lists (`LazyVStack` / `LazyHStack`)

A `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing a `ForEach` is a **windowed data
container**. The app supplies the collection and the row builder; the engine
owns the window and evaluates the builder only for visible rows:

```kotlin
LazyVStack(spacing = 0) {
    ForEach(items) { item, _ ->
        RowView(item)
            .frame(height = 44f)   // fixed main-axis extent
    }
}
```

Rules:

- `ForEach` inside a lazy stack is a **data source**, not an eager child list.
  Outside a lazy stack it keeps its eager behavior.
- The lazy stack's content MUST be exactly one `ForEach` for virtualization;
  other children keep the eager stack behavior.
- `ITEM_COUNT` = the collection size. `ITEM_EXTENT` = the row's fixed main-axis
  size, read from the first realized row's `HEIGHT` (VStack) / `WIDTH` (HStack).
  If the row has no fixed main-axis frame, the author MUST pass an explicit
  `itemExtent` (e.g. `ForEach(items, itemExtent = 44f)`); otherwise the DSL
  reports an authoring error. Every row MUST use the same extent.
- `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` = the window start. The engine sets it; the author does not.
- The DSL sets `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 10 (`VISIBLE_RANGE`) and routes the event
  to the engine's internal window; the author does not manage a window signal.
- The engine reconciles window children by absolute index, or by an optional
  `key` extractor (`ForEach(items, key = { it.id })`); without a key, identity
  is the absolute index.
- Row-local component state is not preserved after a row leaves the window; keep
  row state in the data model (keyed state is a follow-up).
- A full-snapshot/SSR emission carries the first window plus the full virtual
  extent; the client corrects the window after `META::ENVIRONMENT`.

736:**The active platform path is universal** — `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` is an

**The active platform path is universal** — `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` is an
`EnvironmentKey<String>` the host provides for **every** app (with
or without navigation), like SwiftUI's `onOpenURL` generalized across platforms:
```java
// host (always):
WritableSignal<String> activePath = Signals.signal(env.route());
RenderResult result = emitter.mount(
        root.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath))),
        new Environment(state));
// re-route on deep-link/popstate:
activePath.set(env.route());   // or from a NAVIGATE event URL
```
- **An app with navigation** builds a **router bound to the signal**:
  `Navigation.navigator().route(...).build(Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH))`.
  The signal is the source of truth: external writes (deep links/popstate) are
  re-routed **through guards** (never bypassed), and the router's own
  `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace` are mirrored back into the signal when it is
  writable (the host's `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` always is). The initial value is
  guard-processed.
- **An app without navigation** just observes the signal — read it, or register
  a `PathChange` modifier listener (`pathChange(p -> p.listener(path -> …))`)
  (fires on every change, including the initial value).
- `NAVIGATE` events: a URL updates `activePath` (→ bound router re-routes guard-aware,
  `PathChange` listeners fire); a back (no URL) goes to `RenderResult.navigateHandler`
  → `router.pop()` — meaningful only when a router exists.

**Any component can change the route** — declarative navigation intents. A
component anywhere *inside* a `NavigationContainer` can change the route without
threading a `Router` by hand, using the `NavigationIntent` modifier:

```java
Button.make(b -> b.title("Go to kitchen").action(...))
      .modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate("/kitchen"));   // direct selection
Button.make(b -> b.title("Open item").action(...))
      .modifiers(NavigationIntent.push("/item/1"));        // drill-down (back-stack)

- [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
  in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
  or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
  `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
  the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
  scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).

### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)

1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
   Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
   never reuse allocated ids.
2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
   with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
   DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
   appendix.
3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
   carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
   (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
   scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
   (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
