 # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 12, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
 signals/computed/effects, router, cross-platform state, and the
 `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. The opcode/wire layer
 (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`) lives in the
 pure-Java `pathland-core` module, which this module depends on. Server and
 renderer modules depend on this module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored
 views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in
 `pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image
 build) carries no JNA.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Opcode/wire layer**: moved to the `pathland-core` module
   (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`). The DSL
   still re-exports the same behaviour through `Text(...)` and the emitter.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly
   typed `Topic<T, S>` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also
   `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)`
   declares an unscoped `Topic<T, GlobalSubject>` with the two-argument
   `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal<T>` backed by a
   session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and
   applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local,
   installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes
   `unsubscribe` and `submit`. Resolution is lazy when a root view's field
   initializer runs before the context is installed.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop**: moved to `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore`),
   so server runtimes do not pull JNA.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its
   real parent (not the tree root), so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a
   pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal/state and Kotlin DSL tests
   (which exercise the emitter end-to-end); `pathland-core` owns the
   protocol-manifest, frame-codec, and Markdown tests.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `topic(key, subject, initial)`, `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`,
   `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Verification gaps
 
 - **Media swap coverage (MEDIA-COVERAGE-001):** `MediaProjectionTest` covers
   root projection, surface-first binding, root-rerender identity, and transport
   targeting. It does not establish every structural-swap frame invariant or
   native playback continuity. See the
   [traceability pilot audit](../../../docs/audits/media-controller-identity.md).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
-- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` still
-  materialize all children eagerly. The `ForEach` data source, extent
-  inference, engine-owned window, keyed window reconcile,
-  `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/`FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` emission, and `VISIBLE_RANGE`
-  input routing are not implemented.
+- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing
+  a `ForEach` are windowed — extent inference, engine-owned window, keyed
+  window reconcile, the window properties, and `VISIBLE_RANGE` routing are
+  implemented. Gaps: variable-height rows, lazy grids, keyed row-local state
+  across eviction, and focused-row pinning.
 
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-core` is the pure-Java opcode/wire leaf: protocol, frame codec,
   events, opcode sink, attributed text, and Markdown.
 - `pathland-view-core` is the Kotlin engine + DSL module: signal/state/router,
   the `View` SPI and value types, the retained-tree emitter, and
   `dev.pathland.view.dsl`. It depends on `pathland-core`.
 - `core`/`engine`/`dsl` remain logical subpackages inside `pathland-view-core`,
   with a few deliberate intra-module references (`Color`/`MediaController`/
   `Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting the engine out would still
   require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on both modules. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 # pathland-core-transport — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** September 3, 2026
 
 The **transport** layer: the shared-memory ring owner and the network batch
 codec (both directions). Protocol contract: `spec/OPCODE.md` (Transport).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **`RingTransport`**: zero-copy SPSC shared-memory transport over the
   `pathland-core` linear memory — `next_frame` (guest→host frames as
   `OpcodeBatch`) and `send_input`/`drain_events` (host→guest raw inputs,
   including shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` text via the host event arena).
 - **Network batch codec** (`batch.rs`, `net.rs`): `encode_batch`/`decode_batch`
   for guest→host frames and `encode_events`/`decode_events` for host→guest
   event batches (`HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag, `TEXT_CHANGED` text in the
   batch string section, `Navigate` URLs in the string section, plus all typed
   draft events — focus/edit/submit/scroll/wheel/date-changed). Both directions
   are fully wired at the codec level.
 - **Message sequence** (`sequence`, header offset 8): the batch header carries a
   per-stream monotonic **message sequence** (the network transport's loss
   detector; `Batch::sequence()`). The `Batcher` owns the counter and increments
   it once per flushed batch; heartbeat/request batches carry `0`. Consumers
   detect a gap and recover with a full snapshot (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap
   detection).
 - **Batching policy** (`batching.rs`): time/size flush thresholds with arena
   delta tracking.
 - **Conformance vectors 13/14/19** (`conformance.rs`): golden network-batch
   bytes — incl. **vector 19** (a `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` with the
   `"color.primary"` arena delta).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - No out-of-the-box duplex *server transport* (WebSocket/session plumbing) in
   this crate — the codecs exist; the Java demos (Quarkus/Spring) wire the
   browser↔server duplex.

 # pathland-render-core — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The **toolkit-free renderer core shared by every Pathland renderer** (GTK4, Qt,
 …): opcode-frame decode into a retained native-element description
 (`RenderTree` / `HostNode`) plus the design-token resolution contract
 (spec/TOKENS.md). Protocol contract: `spec/`. This crate touches **no toolkit**
 (no GTK, no Qt) — it is pure protocol + tokens.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata decode**: `RenderTree` stores `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (`WindowMeta`), shared by the GTK/Qt renderers; empty strings clear fields.
 
 - **`RenderTree` / `HostNode`** (extracted from `pathland-render-gtk`'s
   `host.rs`, which was already GTK-free):
   - `TREE` ops → node tree: `CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
     `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD` (append/insert at `u32::MAX`), parent/child
     bookkeeping.
   - `STYLE` ops → node properties: `SET_PROPERTY` (numeric `properties`,
     `STRING` resolved from the arena into `strings`, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs kept
     in `token_refs`), `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (global overrides, base +
     `dark.` split), and `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (decoded into
     `HostNode::attributed`, with the plain `text` fallback populated).
   - Node accessors: `node(id)`, `root()`, string/f32/u32 property helpers,
     `checked()`.
 - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
   - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides stored (base + `dark.*` by path
     prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolved from the arena).
   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path and
     **resolve at apply time** against the theme, the active scheme, and the
     parent-fallback chain into concrete `properties`/`strings`
     (`resolve_tokens`, reusing `pathland_core::tokens::resolve_ref`); paths
     are kept for re-resolution on scheme change.
   - Explicit `dark.` references resolve the dark layer in either scheme.
   - Previously materialized token values are removed before each resolution,
     so an unresolvable reference (or a reset override) leaves the property
     unset instead of retaining a stale value. A literal `SET_PROPERTY`
     replaces a previous token reference (and vice versa).
   - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) via `concrete_default_tables` —
     concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks; a renderer may enrich with native
     theme colors via `RenderTree::set_defaults`.
   - Platform scheme (`set_scheme`) and application override
     (`set_scheme_override(Option<Scheme>)`, `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) are
     separate; the effective scheme is the override when set.
   - `reset_theme()` / `META::RESET_THEME` clears base + `dark.*` overrides and
     re-resolves against renderer defaults.
   - `concrete_default_tables` now covers the full `TIER1_TOKENS` catalog in
     both schemes (coverage-tested).
 - **`render_tree_from_frame`** — decode a fresh tree from one frame.
 - **`describe`** — one-opcode human-readable line (debugging aid).
 
 ## Consumed by
 
 - `pathland-render-gtk` (decode + token resolution; the GTK-specific
   `tokens.rs` GTK theme-color enrichment stays in that crate).
 - `pathland-render-qt` (planned).
 - `pathland-view-native` and `pathland-core-transport` dev-tests (decode a
   frame into a `RenderTree` without pulling in a toolkit).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - No layout computation (by design — the protocol never emits rects).
 - No META handling beyond theming (`SET_COLOR_SCHEME`/`RESET_THEME`); `RESET` /
   `ENVIRONMENT` / `RESYNC` remain renderer-owned concerns.
 - Web renderers do not yet implement the parent-path fallback (`font.body` →
   `font.body.size`) in CSS; native renderers do via the shared resolver.
 - **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/
-  `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` are not decoded into `HostNode` yet.
+  `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` decode generically into `HostNode.properties`; no
+  dedicated layout handling lives here.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-render-core` — decode of a declarative frame (no
 layout/rect data present), delta-frame application (unchanged nodes preserved),
 and STRING property resolution from the arena. Full decode/token coverage also
 runs through `pathland-render-gtk`'s tests (`cargo test`).

 /// Emit the token conventions (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`)
 /// from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the pure data + pure functions the
 /// DOM client imports, so the `--pl-*` naming / length rules cannot drift.
 pub fn emit_tokens_core_ts() -> String {
     let mut out = String::new();
     out.push_str(
         "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
          // Canonical design-token conventions from `pathland-render-html::token_spec`\n\
          // (spec/TOKENS.md). Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
     );
     let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
     let list = |items: &[&str]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|s| q(*s)).collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     let pair_list = |items: &[(&str, &str)]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items
             .iter()
             .map(|(a, b)| format!("[{}, {}]", q(*a), q(*b)))
             .collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     writeln!(out, "export const DARK_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::DARK_PREFIX)).unwrap();
     writeln!(out, "export const VAR_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::VAR_PREFIX)).unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX = {};",
         q(token_spec::FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(out, "export const SPACE_FAMILY = {};", q(token_spec::SPACE_FAMILY)).unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_PREFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIXES)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = {};",
         pair_list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_EXACT: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_EXACT)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
         list(token_spec::LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES)
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "\n/** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` → `-`.\n \
          *  The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the same\n \
          *  variable inside a media query. */\n\
          export function tokenToCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 return VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */\n\
          export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
          \x20 return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The forced-dark variable for a token path (`--pl-dark-<path>`). */\n\
          export function tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 return FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`). */\n\
          export function isLengthToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
          \x20 for (const prefix of LENGTH_PREFIXES) {\n\
          \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix)) return true;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 for (const [prefix, suffix] of LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX) {\n\
          \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix) && path.endsWith(suffix)) return true;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 if (LENGTH_EXACT.includes(path)) return true;\n\
          \x20 return path.startsWith(\"elevation.\") && LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES.some((s) => path.endsWith(s));\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** Resolve a `DESIGN_TOKEN` property reference to a CSS expression: the\n\
           *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;\n\
           *  an explicit `dark.` reference uses the forced-dark variable family; every\n\
           *  other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>, unset)`. */\n\
          export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {\n\
          \x20 const forcedDark = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
          \x20 const bare = forcedDark ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
          \x20 if (bare.startsWith(SPACE_FAMILY)) {\n\
          \x20\x20 const rest = bare.slice(SPACE_FAMILY.length);\n\
          \x20\x20 if (rest.length > 0 && !Number.isNaN(Number(rest))) {\n\
          \x20\x20\x20 const base = forcedDark ? \"--pl-dark-space-base\" : \"--pl-space-base\";\n\
          \x20\x20\x20 return `calc(var(${base}) * ${rest})`;\n\
          \x20\x20 }\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 if (forcedDark) {\n\
          \x20\x20 return `var(${tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return `var(${tokenToCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
          }\n",
     );
     out
 }
 
 /// Emit the role→semantic-element conventions (`generated/role-spec.ts`) from
 /// `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — the single source the Rust SSR renderer
 /// and the DOM client share for semantic tags / ARIA fallbacks.
 pub fn emit_role_spec_ts() -> String {
     let mut out = String::new();
     out.push_str(
         "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
          // Canonical ROLE → semantic HTML element mapping from\n\
          // `pathland-render-html::role_spec` (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties).\n\
          // Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
     );
     let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
     let nums = |items: &[u16]| {
         let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|v| format!("{v:#06x}")).collect();
         format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
     };
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const GENERIC_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
         nums(role_spec::GENERIC_COMPONENTS)
     )
     .unwrap();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
         nums(role_spec::NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS)
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "export interface RoleTag {\n\
          \x20 role: number;\n\
          \x20 tag: string;\n\
          \x20 aria: string;\n\
          }\n\n",
     );
     out.push_str("export const ROLE_TAGS: readonly RoleTag[] = [\n");
     for rt in role_spec::ROLE_TAGS {
         writeln!(out, "  {{ role: {}, tag: {}, aria: {} }},", rt.role, q(rt.tag), q(rt.aria)).unwrap();
     }
     out.push_str("];\n\n");
     let heading_pairs: Vec<String> = role_spec::HEADING_STYLES
         .iter()
         .map(|(style, level)| format!("[{style}, {level}]"))
         .collect();
     writeln!(
         out,
         "export const HEADING_STYLES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [{}];",
         heading_pairs.join(", ")
     )
     .unwrap();
     out.push_str(
         "\n/** The heading level a `TEXT_STYLE` typography implies, or null for the\n \
          *  non-heading styles (Subheadline, Body, Caption, …). */\n\
          export function headingLevel(textStyle: number): number | null {\n\
          \x20 const found = HEADING_STYLES.find(([s]) => s === textStyle);\n\
          \x20 return found ? found[1] : null;\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The heading element tag for a level (1 → `h1` … 5 → `h5`). */\n\
          export function headingTag(level: number): string {\n\
          \x20 return \"h\" + String(level);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** A shell's role behavior (see `pathland-render-html::role_spec`).\n \
           *  Generic `div`/`span` shells may be retagged; native controls convey\n \
           *  their own role; anything else only gets an ARIA attribute. */\n\
          export type ShellKind = \"generic\" | \"native\" | \"other\";\n\n\
          /** The semantic tag a `(shell kind, role)` pair resolves to, or null. */\n\
          export function semanticTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind !== \"generic\") return null;\n\
          \x20 const found = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
          \x20 return found ? found.tag : null;\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The effective tag for a generic TEXT shell: a heading `TEXT_STYLE`\n\
           *  wins (always a heading), then the semantic role (`ROLE_HEADER` → `<h2>`,\n\
           *  `ROLE_PARAGRAPH` → `<p>`, landmarks), else null (→ `<span>`). */\n\
          export function textTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number, textStyle: number | null): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind === \"generic\" && textStyle !== null) {\n\
          \x20\x20 const level = headingLevel(textStyle);\n\
          \x20\x20 if (level !== null) return headingTag(level);\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return semanticTag(kind, role);\n\
          }\n\n\
          /** The ARIA `role` value to emit for `(shell kind, role)`, or null when\n\
           *  the element already conveys the role (a semantic tag or a native control). */\n\
          export function ariaRole(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
          \x20 if (kind === \"native\") return null;\n\
          \x20 const tagged = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
          \x20 if (tagged) {\n\
          \x20\x20 return kind === \"generic\" ? null : tagged.aria;\n\
          \x20 }\n\
          \x20 return null;\n\
          }\n",
     );
     out
 }
 
 fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
     let consts = constants_ts_path();
     std::fs::write(&consts, emit_constants_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", consts.display());
     let tokens = tokens_core_ts_path();
     if let Some(parent) = tokens.parent() {
         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
     }
     std::fs::write(&tokens, emit_tokens_core_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", tokens.display());
     let roles = role_spec_ts_path();
     if let Some(parent) = roles.parent() {
         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
     }
     std::fs::write(&roles, emit_role_spec_ts())?;
     println!("wrote {}", roles.display());
     Ok(())
 }

 # pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
 Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata constants**: `CMD_SET_WINDOW_METADATA` + `WINDOW_TITLE/DESCRIPTION/LOCALE` are generated from `pathland_core`.
 - **Attributed text**: `CMD_SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` is generated from
   `pathland_core::parameter`.
 
 - **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
   bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
   revalue changes the emitted file); the protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
   shape kind, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/` — `ROLE_*` is bound to
   `pathland_core::constants::role` (the semantic-only catalog, dense 0–13) and
   `TEXT_STYLE_*` to `pathland_core::constants::text_style`.
 - **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
   the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `tokenToForcedDarkCssVar`,
   `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables)
   emitted from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust
   renderer and the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it. Explicit
   `dark.` references resolve to `--pl-dark-…` and plain refs carry the
   `unset` fallback.
 - **`generated/role-spec.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/role-spec.ts`):
   the semantic `ROLE` → element + typography → heading conventions emitted from
   `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — `ROLE_TAGS`, `HEADING_STYLES`,
   `ShellKind`, and the `semanticTag`/`textTag`/`ariaRole`/`headingLevel`
   resolvers — so semantic-tag / ARIA / heading decisions cannot drift between
   the Rust SSR renderer and the DOM client. `constants.ts` also carries the
   media surface (`COMPONENT_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`/`VIDEO`, `PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE`/
   `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_*` event commands) and the icon surface (`COMPONENT_ICON`,
   `PROP_ICON_NAME`).
 - **Icon glyph map — intentionally NOT generated.** The full canonical icon
   catalog (`generated/icons.ts`, ~13KB in the bundle) was **removed**: the DOM
   client no longer carries glyph data. SSR inlines only the icons the page uses,
   and a runtime swap to a name the page did not embed lazily fetches
   `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the host — which serves it from the shared
   Rust renderer (`pathland_html_icon_svg`, the same `pathland-render-html::icons`
   source SSR inlines from), so glyph parity between SSR and the client is
   guaranteed by the single Rust source, not by a mirrored TS map.
 - **`npm run regen`** (`lib/typescript/scripts/regen.mjs`) runs both generators
   (and the golden-fixture emitter); CI's `rust` job runs them and fails on
   `git diff --exit-code` drift.
 
 ## Regenerate
 
 `npm run regen` (from `lib/typescript`) or `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`
 (from `lib/rust`), then commit the generated files with the change that produced
 them.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - Theme/scheme **runtime** behavior is handled by `apply.ts` + `tokens.ts`,
   not generated. Only the pure-data surfaces are generated. The element-shell factory
   (`elements.ts`) and the property-handler table (`classes.ts`) are still
   hand-written — their alignment is enforced behaviorally by the
   `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness rather than generated. Extending
   the generator to those tables is the planned next step.

internal class ForEachView<T>(
    private val items: Signal<List<T>>,
    private val keyOf: ((T) -> Any)?,
    internal val itemExtent: Float?,
    private val content: PathlandScope.(T, Int) -> Unit,
) : View {
    fun items(): List<T> = items.get()
    fun row(index: Int, list: List<T>): View = rowView { content(list[index], index) }
    fun key(index: Int, list: List<T>): Any = keyOf?.invoke(list[index]) ?: index
    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
        val node = PathlandNode(Components.VSTACK)
        val list = items.get()
        list.forEachIndexed { index, item ->
            node.children.add(rowView { content(item, index) }.render(env))
        }
        return node
    }
}
```

private fun initialWindow(count: Int, extent: Float, vertical: Boolean): IntRange {
    if (count == 0) return IntRange.EMPTY

private class LazyStackView(
    private val component: Int,
    private val vertical: Boolean,
    private val data: ForEachView<*>,
    private val alignment: Signal<*>?,
    private val spacing: Signal<Float>?,
    private val spacingValue: Float?,
) : View {
    private var window: WritableSignal<IntRange>? = null

    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
        val node = PathlandNode(component)
        alignment?.let { node.property(Properties.ALIGNMENT, it) }
        if (spacing != null) node.property(Properties.SPACING, spacing)
        else if (spacingValue != null) node.properties[Properties.SPACING] = spacingValue

        val list = data.items()
        val count = list.size
        val emitter = Emitter.current()
        val inheritedExtent = emitter?.currentSlotOldLazyExtent()
        val extent = data.itemExtent ?: inheritedExtent ?: inferExtent(data, env, vertical)
        val inheritedWindow = emitter?.currentSlotOldLazyWindow()
        val windowSignal = window ?: inheritedWindow ?: Signals.signal(IntRange.EMPTY)
        window = windowSignal
        if (windowSignal.get().isEmpty() && count > 0) {
            Signals.untracked { windowSignal.set(initialWindow(count, extent, vertical)); null }
        }
        val raw = windowSignal.get()
        val first = raw.first.coerceIn(0, (count - 1).coerceAtLeast(0))
        val end = raw.last.coerceIn(first, (count - 1).coerceAtLeast(0))
        if (first != raw.first || end != raw.last) {
            Signals.untracked { windowSignal.set(first..end); null }
        }

        node.properties[Properties.ITEM_COUNT] = count
        node.properties[Properties.ITEM_EXTENT] = extent
        node.properties[Properties.FIRST_ITEM_INDEX] = first
        node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] =
            (node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] as? Int ?: 0) or Commands.Listeners.VISIBLE_RANGE
        node.lazyWindow = windowSignal
        node.lazyExtent = extent
        node.visibleRangeInput = VisibleRangeInput { firstVisible, visibleCount ->
            val total = data.items().size
            val start = (firstVisible - OVERSCAN).coerceAtLeast(0)
            val last = (firstVisible + visibleCount + OVERSCAN).coerceAtMost(total) - 1
            if (total > 0 && last >= start) {
                windowSignal.set(start..last)
            } else {
                windowSignal.set(IntRange.EMPTY)
            }
        }

        val keys = ArrayList<Any>(end - first + 1)
        val nodes = LinkedHashMap<Any, PathlandNode>()
        for (index in first..end) {
            val key = data.key(index, list)
            keys.add(key)
            val child = data.row(index, list).render(env)
            node.children.add(child)
            nodes[key] = child
        }
        node.lazyKeys = keys
        node.lazyNodes = nodes
        return node
    }
}

The `ForEachView<*>` methods `row(index, list: List<T>)` and `key` use the captured type `T`; calling with `List<Any?>` (from `data.items()`) doesn't match `List<CapturedType(*)`. We need to make the `ForEachView` API accept `List<*>` or use a non-generic interface. Simplest: make `ForEachView` non-generic internally by storing `itemsSignal: Signal<List<*>>` and casting. Or add methods that don't take the list:
- `fun row(index: Int): View` reads `items()` internally.
- `fun key(index: Int): Any` reads internally.
- `fun count(): Int`.
But the `LazyStackView` needs the list for the key/row; it can call `data.items()` and then use non-generic methods. The generic type is only for the content lambda. We can store the content as `(Any?, Int) -> Unit`? The content is typed `PathlandScope.(T, Int) -> Unit`; inside `ForEachView<T>`, we can keep it and expose non-generic methods:
```kotlin
fun items(): List<T> = itemsSignal.get()
fun count(): Int = items().size
fun row(index: Int): View { val list = items(); return rowView { content(list[index], index) } }
fun key(index: Int): Any { val list = items(); return keyOf?.invoke(list[index]) ?: index }
```
The `LazyStackView` calls `data.items()` (returns `List<*>`), `data.row(index)`, `data.key(index)`. The `data.row` internally reads the signal again (fine) and uses the typed content. This avoids passing `List<*>` into generic methods.
- `inferExtent` uses `data.row(0)`.
- The `LazyStackView` reads `list` for count, but `row`/`key` read it again. That's fine; the signal read is tracked (same value).
- To avoid multiple signal reads, we can add `fun row(index: Int, list: List<T>)` but expose a non-generic `fun rowAt(index: Int): View`. Simpler: use `row(index)`.

Let me change `ForEachView`:
```kotlin
fun count(): Int = itemsSignal.get().size
fun row(index: Int): View {
    val list = itemsSignal.get()
    return rowView { content(list[index], index) }
}
fun key(index: Int): Any {
    val list = itemsSignal.get()
    return keyOf?.invoke(list[index]) ?: index
}
```
Keep `items()` for the `LazyStackView` count/list? We can use `count()` and `row(index)`/`key(index)`. The `LazyStackView` needs the list only for `row`/`key`; remove the list variable except for count. Use `val count = data.count()`. But `data.count()` reads the signal; the lazy component subscribes. Good.
- `inferExtent(data, env, vertical)` uses `data.row(0)`.
- The `visibleRangeInput` uses `data.count()`.
- The eager `renderNode` uses `itemsSignal.get()`.

But first, let me consider a critical bug: the `LazyStackView` `inferExtent` uses `data.row(0).renderNode(env)`. If the row is a `Component`, `renderNode` resolves `body()`. But `Component.body()` may read signals and subscribe the **current** tracked context. We wrapped in `Signals.untracked`, so no subscription. Good.

But `data.row(0)` calls `itemsSignal.get()` outside `Signals.untracked`? In `inferExtent`, `data.row(0)` is inside `Signals.untracked { ... }`, so the signal read is untracked. Good. However, `data.row(0)` also calls `rowView { content(...) }`, which may read signals; untracked. Fine.

Another critical issue: `LazyStackView.renderNode` calls `data.count()` and `data.row(index)`; `data.row` reads the items signal. If the list changes between `count()` and `row`, the index might be out of bounds. In a single render, the signal is stable. Fine.

Another issue: the `initialWindow` uses `Environment.value(Platform.VIEWPORT).get()`. The `Environment.value` static reads the current scope. If no viewport is bound, `EnvironmentSignal.get()` returns `captured?.get() as T` where `captured` is null → returns null cast to `Viewport`; this is an unchecked cast that may return null at runtime. The local `val viewport: Viewport?` handles it. Good.

Another issue: the `windowSignal` is `WritableSignal<IntRange>`. `Signals.signal(IntRange.EMPTY)` returns `WritableSignal<IntRange>`. The `IntRange` is a Kotlin type; the signal store may require a `Signal` value type. Fine.

Another issue: The `LazyStackView` `window` field persists across re-renders of the same view instance. On a parent re-render, a new `LazyStackView` is created; it recovers `inheritedWindow` from `oldNodeHint`. But `oldNodeHint` is set only if the lazy view is a child of a parent. If the lazy view is the root, a parent re-render doesn't happen; the root slot's view is the same. Fine.

Another issue: When the parent re-renders, the `LazyStackView` new instance has `window = null`, `inheritedWindow` is the old node's `lazyWindow`. It uses it. Good. The `windowSignal` is shared. The old node's `lazyWindow` is the same signal. Good.

Another issue: The `LazyStackView` sets `node.lazyWindow = windowSignal` and `node.lazyExtent = extent`. On `reconcileNode`, the old node's `lazyWindow` is non-null and fresh's is non-null, so `reconcileLazyChildren` runs. Good.

Another issue: `reconcileLazyChildren` uses `fresh.lazyKeys` and `fresh.lazyNodes`; the `LazyStackView` sets them. Good.

Another issue: On the first mount, `assignIds(tree)` assigns ids to all children. The `lazyNodes` map keys→nodes point to the same objects. Good. But `reconcileLazyChildren` on a re-render compares `old.lazyNodes` (old nodes) and `fresh.lazyNodes`. The old node's `lazyNodes` map was set during the previous render. Good.

Another issue: The `LazyStackView` sets `node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS]` to the bit. But `ensureBindingId` may also set `BINDING_ID` for text inputs; fine.

Another issue: The `visibleRangeInput` closure calls `windowSignal.set(...)`. This writes the signal, which triggers the lazy component's re-render (the signal is read during render). The write happens on the event dispatch thread; the emitter/session actor? In the JVM server, the `InputDispatcher.dispatch` runs on the session actor (via `PathlandSession.dispatch`), so the write triggers a synchronous flush and re-render. Good. In the desktop demo, the host loop dispatches events and re-renders; the signal write triggers the emitter? The desktop demo uses the emitter and a render loop; the signal flush is synchronous. Good.

```kotlin
@Test
fun lazyStackEmitsAWindowedDataSource() {
    val items = signal((0 until 100).map { "item-$it" })
    val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
    val emitter = Emitter(sink)
    val result = emitter.mount(
        LazyVStack(spacing = 0f) {
            ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text(item).frame(height = 44f) }
        },
        Environment.DEFAULT,
    )
    val frame = sink.frame()
    val props = frame.opcodes().filter { it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY }
    fun value(id: Int): Int? = props.firstOrNull { (it.b() and 0xffff) == id }?.c()
    assertEquals(100, value(Properties.ITEM_COUNT))
    assertEquals(44f, Float.fromBits(value(Properties.ITEM_EXTENT)!!))
    assertEquals(0, value(Properties.FIRST_ITEM_INDEX))
    // initial window is 20 items (DEFAULT_WINDOW) + 2 overscan = 22

Let me at least implement the GTK virtual extent (spacers) without the visible-range reporting, so the desktop shows the correct scroll extent and window position. The visible range reporting is needed for the window to move on scroll; without it, the app's window stays at the initial 0..21 and scrolling shows blank. So spacers alone aren't enough. Implementing the full GTK handler is necessary for a working desktop. Let me attempt a minimal GTK implementation.

**GTK visible range reporting:**

Add to `Renderer`:
- `lazy_info: HashMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<LazyInfo>>>`
- `lazy_spacers: HashMap<u32, Vec<gtk::Widget>>`
- `lazy_attached: HashSet<u32>`

`LazyInfo`:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct LazyInfo {
    count: u32,
    extent: f32,
    first: u32,
    spacing: f32,
    vertical: bool,
    last_first: u32,
    last_count: u32,
}
```
Use `Rc<RefCell<LazyInfo>>`.

In `sync_stack_children`:
- Remove old spacers (if any) at the start.
- After `reconcile_box_children`, if lazy, add spacers and update the info.
- Attach the range handler once per lazy node. The handler needs the scroll view. We can attach it when the widget is created/updated in `update` (where `attach_control_events` is called). At that point, the widget may not yet be inside the scroll view (the parent hierarchy is being built). We can attach on a `size_allocate`/`map` signal, or defer via `glib::idle_add_local`. Simpler: attach on the lazy box's `map` signal (when it becomes visible), find the scroll ancestor, and connect. Use a `Once` flag in the info (`attached: bool`).
- The handler:
  - On adjustment `value_changed`/`changed` and box `size_allocate`, compute the range and send if changed.
  - The scroll view may be the lazy box's direct parent or an ancestor. Find `widget.ancestor(gtk::ScrolledWindow::static_type())` and downcast.
  - The content offset: assume the lazy box is the direct child of the scroll view. If not, compute the box's position relative to the scroll view's child using `box.compute_point(&scroll_child, &Point::new(0,0))`. In GTK4, `Widget::compute_point(&self, target: &impl IsA<Widget>, point: &graphene::Point) -> Option<graphene::Point>`. The scroll view's child is `sw.child()`. The point (0,0) in the box's coordinates maps to the child's coordinates; the child's coordinate space includes the full content. The scroll offset is `adj.value()`. So the box's content offset = `point.y()`. The visible range start relative to the box = `adj.value() - point.y()`, end = start + `adj.page_size()`.
  - For a direct child, `point.y() = 0`.
  - Compute `first = floor(start/stride)`, `end = ceil(end/stride)`, count = end-first.
  - Send `Event::VisibleRange { target, first_index: first, count }`.
  - Update `last_first/last_count` in the info to avoid duplicate sends.
- The `event_sink` is `self.event_sink`; pass a clone to the handler.
- The handler captures the `Rc<RefCell<LazyInfo>>`, the `target`, and the `sink`.

 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,

 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.

Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.

 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.

   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates
   `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
   drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
   `builtin_css_name()`); the Java port copies the same committed assets into
   its jar via Maven resources (`BaseCss`).
 - The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
   (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
   emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - The Maven `refresh-ide` profile and CI run the design build + sync. Do not
   edit generated CSS by hand.
 
 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Kotlin DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Kotlin DSL
 (`dev.pathland.nativecore` in `pathland-native-core`) binds it with **JNA**
 (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - The Java/Kotlin desktop demo (`pathland-desktop-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk`
   as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Kotlin view's
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared view the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Kotlin JVM authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`, in `lib/java/pathland-view-core`)
 
 The **sole JVM authoring surface**. It is the SwiftUI-like DSL shared by desktop,
 Spring Boot, Quarkus, and web apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open Kotlin interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code defines its own views by
   extending `Component` or implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()`; a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later write
   re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound
   to a node stays fine-grained and does not re-run the body. Plain
   `if`/`when`/`for` works; `ForEach` is the reactive list component.
 - **Builders and modifiers**: `VStack(spacing = 8f) { … }`, `Text("hi")`,
   `Button("Save") { … }`, `.padding`, `.frame`, `.fontSize`, `.background`,
   `.buttonStyle(BorderedButtonStyle)`, `.windowMetadata`, navigation intents, and
   the full modifier vocabulary. Styles are Kotlin values
   (`PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`).
 - **Builder scopes**: view blocks take a `PathlandScope` receiver. `PathlandScope`,
   `Navigation.Builder`, and modifier/style `Config` receivers share the
   `@PathlandDsl` marker, so an outer router/config receiver cannot be captured
   implicitly inside a nested view block (compile-time guard only; the
   thread-local `ViewScopes` stack still collects children).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` provides `val count by state(0)` (auto-keyed
   by property name) or `state(0, "key")`, bound to the session's
   `PersistentState` before the first `body()` render — no annotation processor or
   kapt.
 - **Java hosting**: Java Spring Boot/Quarkus apps remain first-class hosts. A
   Java `PathlandApp` bean returns a Kotlin `View`
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`); no Kotlin compiler or authoring DSL is
   needed in the host module. Every reusable Kotlin root exposes a public
   constructor or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factory with Java-friendly types.
 - **Consistency** with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the
   emitter/HTML tests (golden byte layout + round-trips).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 Rationale: [ADR-0009](./docs/decisions/0009-cross-language-conformance.md).
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→JVM source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005

 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Kotlin DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
 5. If emission behavior changed, run
    `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
 6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
 7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.

 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

 # pathland-desktop-demo — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 5, 2026
 
 Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
 `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
 (`libpathland_gtk`, `dev.pathland.demo.gtk.GtkHost`) or the **Qt Quick renderer**
 (`libpathland_qt`, `dev.pathland.demo.qt.QtHost`) — the cross-language,
 shared-renderer story. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## How it works
 
 - The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
   `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink` from `pathland-native-core`,
   **zero-copy**).
 - The in-process renderer pumps the same ring in place
   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` / `pathland_qt_run_ring`); no
   `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
 - Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that the host drains
   (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
   shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
   router back).
 - State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
   over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
 - **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks and reports
   `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against a local asset root: the demo
   extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` jar
   at startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls the renderer's
   `set_asset_root`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **`GtkRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` + `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); library resolved
   from `pathland.gtk.lib` or `java.library.path`.
 - **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_qt`
   (`pathland_qt_run_ring` + `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`); library resolved
   from `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
 - **`RingEventReader`** (shared, `dev.pathland.demo.desktop`) — decodes raw ring
   `EVENT` opcodes into `dev.pathland.core.transport.Event`, resolving
   `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings from the shared host → guest event arena
   (header `0x40`), plus `MEDIA_*` and `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit
   sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot swaps to its wide candidate).
 - **`GtkHost`** (`main`) — Java host; mounts the Apple Music-style player,
   extracts the demo assets, runs GTK (1180×800), drains and dispatches events.
 - **`QtHost`** (`main`) — Kotlin host; mounts the player, extracts the demo
   assets, runs Qt Quick, drains and dispatches events.
 - The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
   GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **GTK playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed;
   without it the app runs but the pipeline errors on play.
 - The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
   `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
   `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
 - Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the Qt renderer.
 - macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` for both hosts.
 - No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in the Rust crates).
-- `RingEventReader` does not decode `VISIBLE_RANGE` (0x15), so lazy-stack
-  windowing is not routed to the app (ADR-0014).
+- `RingEventReader` decodes `VISIBLE_RANGE` (0x15); both GTK and Qt lazy-stack
+  windowing are wired.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test -pl pathland-desktop-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (headless, no GTK/Qt;
 pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and bounds behaviour).
 Manual: `scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` and `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.
